CN: 4 Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Willpower Bonus days

The target needs no food or drink for the duration. Excretion continues normally, with green waste.

entries.name: Forest of Thorns
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Willpower yards Target: AoE (Willpower Bonus yards) Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Target only earth to grow thorny brambles and vines throughout the area. Anyone without Arcane Magic (Life) who crosses on foot must pass Hard (-2 SL) Athletics or gain 1 Bleeding Condition and 1 Entangled Condition with Strength equal to your Willpower. The plants remain after the Spell ends, but lose their magic.

entries.name: Lie of the Land
entries.text:
CN: 5 Range: Initiative Bonus miles Target: You Duration: Special

Touch earth and commune for 1 minute to learn a mental map of natural features in range, including terrain, forests and rivers. Settlements may appear indirectly as cleared ground or trenches. Extending range by Overcasting adds 1 minute of communion per SL.

entries.name: Lifebloom
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: Special Duration: Instant

Restore a blighted or desolate target. Examples: restart a dry river; cleanse and refill a dry or polluted well; instantly ripen every crop in a planted field, vineyard or orchard; or cure all diseases in a sick or unproductive domestic animal and restore its vigour.

entries.name: Regenerate
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Give the target Regeneration (page 360).

entries.name: Banishment
entries.text:
CN: 12 Range: You Target: AoE (Willpower Bonus yards) Duration: Instant

Affect creatures in the area only if their Toughness is below your Willpower. Those with Daemonic or Undead gain Unstable (page 363); if already Unstable, reduce them to 0 Wounds instead.

entries.name: Blinding Light
entries.text:
CN: 5 Range: You Target: You Duration: Instant

Everyone looking at you within WPB yards gains 3 Blinded Conditions, except those with Arcane Magic (Light).

entries.name: Clarity of Thought
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Intelligence minutes

The target ignores penalties affecting mental processes for the duration, including those from Stunned, Mental Mutations and Psychologies.

entries.name: Daemonbane
entries.text:
CN: 10 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: 1 Daemon Duration: Instant

If the Daemon’s Toughness is higher than your Intelligence but less than double, halve its maximum Wounds until the encounter ends. If lower, banish it. Everyone looking at a banished Daemon from Willpower yards away gains 3 Blinded Conditions unless they have Arcane Magic (Light).

entries.name: Healing Light
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: 1 Duration: Instant

Heal the target Intelligence Bonus Wounds and remove poisons and intoxicants. Passing Very Hard (-3 SL) Channelling (Hysh) also removes 1 Corruption Point gained during the past hour.

entries.name: Net of Amyntok
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: Intelligence Bonus yards Target: 1 Duration: Intelligence Bonus Rounds

The target loses its Move and gains +1 Stunned Condition that cannot be removed while the Spell lasts. Use Intelligence rather than Endurance when recovering from that Condition. Bestial creatures are immune.

entries.name: Phâ’s Protection
entries.text:
CN: 10 Range: You Target: AoE (Willpower Bonus yards) Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Creatures with Daemonic, Undead or mutations cannot enter the area. Any already inside gain 1 Broken Condition until they leave. No creature in the area can gain Corruption Points while the Spell lasts.

entries.name: Speed of Thought
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: You Target: You Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Gain +20 Intelligence and Initiative for the duration.

entries.name: Crucible of Chamon
entries.text:
CN: 7 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: 1 object Duration: Instant

Melt one non-magical metal object, such as a weapon or armour piece covering one body part; it cools almost at once. Held objects are dropped. If worn, it deals its wearer a Damage +WPB magic missile-like hit that ignores Armour Points. The object is destroyed, but its metal retains its base value and remains usable as a smith’s raw material.

entries.name: Enchant Weapon
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: 1 yard Target: Special Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Give one non-magical weapon +WPB Damage, Magical and Unbreakable (pages 304–305) for the duration. Each +3 SL may also add 1 Weapon Quality or remove 1 Weapon Flaw until the Spell ends.

entries.name: Feather of Lead
entries.text:
CN: 5 Range: Willpower yards Target: Area of Effect (Willpower Bonus yards) Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Choose one effect for everyone in the area: count as two steps more Overburdened, or ignore being Overburdened. See Encumbrance, page 299.

entries.name: Fool’s Gold
entries.text:
CN: 4 Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Willpower minutes

Turn all metal in one non-magical metal object into real gold for the duration, then restore the original metal. The change may ruin weapons, make armour unwearably heavy or alter the apparent value of lead coins.

entries.name: Forge of Chamon
entries.text:
CN: 9 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: Special Duration: Willpower minutes

Add 1 Item Quality to a metal item or remove 1 Item Flaw. Each +2 SL allows another Quality added or Flaw removed.

entries.name: Glittering Robe
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: You Target: You Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Shed candelabra-strength light and gain +2 AP at all Locations. Enemies Engaged with you must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance or gain 1 Blinded Condition.

entries.name: Mutable Metal
entries.text:
CN: 5 Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Touch a non-magical metal object to warm and soften it enough to bend or distort with bare hands. With GM agreement, make a relevant Average (+2 SL) Art or Trade Test for a more complex alteration.

entries.name: Transmutation of Chamon
entries.text:
CN: 12 Range: Willpower yards Target: AoE (Willpower Bonus yards) Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Every target in the area suffers a Damage +WPB magic missile that ignores TB and AP, and +1 each of Blinded, Deafened and Stunned lasting for the duration. Affected targets also gain +1 AP and suffer Suffocation (page 169). A target dying during the Spell remains permanently encased in base metal.

entries.name: Choking Shadows
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: 1 Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

The target gains 1 Fatigued Condition, cannot speak and suffers Suffocation (page 169).

entries.name: Doppelganger
entries.text:
CN: 10 Range: You Target: You Duration: Intelligence Bonus minutes

Assume the appearance of another humanoid you know, subject to GM judgment. Anyone without Second Sight is fooled by the appearance, though incorrect mannerisms may give you away. Second Sight users must beat your Casting Test with Opposed Difficult (-1 SL) Intuition to recognise the disguise.

entries.name: Illusion
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: Willpower yards Target: AoE (Intelligence Bonus yards) Duration: Intelligence minutes

Fill the area with an illusory image of your choice. Anyone without Second Sight is automatically fooled. Second Sight users must beat your Casting Test with Opposed Difficult (-1 SL) Intuition to recognise the illusion; success neither ends it nor allows sight through it. The image is normally static. Spend an Action and pass Hard (-2 SL) Channelling (Ulgu) to animate it within its space for that Round.

entries.name: Mindslip
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: 1 yard Target: 1 Duration: Intelligence minutes

Erase the target’s prior memories of you for the duration. When the Spell ends, you may require Opposed Average (+2 SL) Intelligence against your Casting Test; unless the target wins, the memory loss persists until dispelled.

entries.name: Mystifying Miasma
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Willpower yards Target: AoE (Willpower Bonus yards) Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Everyone in the mist without Arcane Magic (Shadows) gains 1 each of Blinded, Deafened and Fatigued for the duration. When affected creatures try to use their Move, they must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Perception or fall Prone.

entries.name: Shadowsteed
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: 1 Duration: Until the next dawn

Summon a riding horse (page 327). Outside sunlight it gains Dark Vision, Ethereal, Fear 1, Magical, Painless and Ward 9+ (page 356), and remains rideable while insubstantial. Riding it grants +2 SL to Ride Tests for riders with Arcane Magic (Shadow), or -2 SL without that Talent. It needs neither rest nor sustenance. At dawn’s first light it dissolves; if ridden when the Spell ends, its rider falls and takes falling damage (page 169).

entries.name: Shadowstep
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: Willpower yards Target: You Duration: Instant

Instantly relocate up to Willpower yards away. Enemies Engaging you at departure gain Surprised.

entries.name: Shroud of Invisibility
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Make the target invisible and imperceptible to mundane senses, automatically fooling anyone without Second Sight. Second Sight users must beat the Casting Test with Opposed Perception to detect someone nearby, without learning an exact position. The target remains perceptible to other senses. The Spell ends when the target attracts attention by loud noise or an attack.

entries.name: Goodwill
entries.text:
CN: 0 Range: You Target: AoE (Fellowship Bonus yards) Duration: Willpower Bonus minutes

Grant +1 SL to every Fellowship Test in the area and suppress the effects of Animosity and Hatred.

entries.name: Halétha’s Joy
entries.text:
CN: 0 Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Fellowship Bonus hours

If biologically possible, the target conceives a child while the Spell lasts. The Spell ends once used.

entries.name: Mirkride
entries.text:
CN: 0 Range: You Target: You Duration: Willpower Bonus minutes

Your spirit enters the Hedge with Ethereal (page 358), observing the material world invisibly and silently but unable to affect it. Your body stays immobile and insensate. Any Magical damage you take ends the Spell instead. You and spirits, other Ethereal beings and Daemons can see and interact with each other, including when invisible. When the Spell ends, your spirit returns to your body. If the body is killed while you are in the Hedge, your spirit wanders forever.

entries.name: Nepenthe
entries.text:
CN: 0 Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: Willpower Bonus hours

Create a silver liquid in a cup. Anyone drinking it within the duration may permanently erase all memory of one individual.

entries.name: Nostrum
entries.text:
CN: 0 Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: Dexterity Bonus hours

Enchant a prepared draught. Drinking it while the Spell lasts immediately heals Dexterity Bonus Wounds and cures one disease chosen by the GM. Each +2 SL may cure an additional disease.

entries.name: Part the Branches
entries.text:
CN: 0 Range: You Target: You Duration: Initiative minutes

See every invisible creature for the duration.

entries.name: Protective Charm
entries.text:
CN: 0 Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: Willpower Bonus days

Enchant a small piece of jewellery or pocket-sized trinket. Its bearer gains +2 SL to resist magical effects and Corruption.

entries.name: Shepherd’s Eye
entries.text:
CN: 0 Range: Special Target: Special Duration: Instant

Place organic material from one creature, such as wool, blood or droppings, in a bowl of water. Scry for 10 - IB minutes; the GM describes that creature’s location through symbols. If the location is familiar, you know where the creature is.

entries.name: Blight
entries.text:
CN: 14 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: Special Duration: Instant

Blight a target, with these examples: all food and drink in a tavern spoil immediately; a well becomes brackish and stagnant; planted crops in a field rot overnight; or a domestic animal sickens, produces nothing useful, develops an unusable coat or hide, and dies in 10 - SL days.

entries.name: Creeping Menace
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Willpower yards Target: 1 Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Each affected target is immediately Engaged by a swarm of your choice of Giant Rats, Giant Spiders or Snakes; use that creature’s standard profile with Swarm added. Spend an Action and pass Challenging (+0 SL) Charm Animal to send one or more swarms against another target. Remaining swarms disappear when the Spell ends.

entries.name: Curse of Crippling Pain
entries.text:
CN: 10 Range: Willpower yards Target: 1 Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Stab a doll or puppet representing the target and choose a Hit Location:
- Body: +1 Fatigued; pass Hard (-2 SL) Endurance or fall Prone.
- Head: 1 Stunned; pass Average (+2 SL) Endurance or gain -SL additional Stunned.
- Limb: rendered useless as though amputated (page 177).
Fatigued and Stunned persist for the duration. Spend an Action and pass Average (+2 SL) Channelling to stab another, previously unaffected Location.

entries.name: Curse of Ill Fortune
entries.text:
CN: 8 Target: 1 Range: Willpower yards or Willpower Bonus miles (with ingredient) Duration: Willpower Bonus minutes or days (with ingredient)

Cause minor inconveniences such as broken laces or chairs, impose -1 SL on every Test, and prevent the target spending Fortune. If they have no Fortune, they must reroll every Test roll of 01–05. Using something belonging to the target, such as a possession or hair, as the ingredient removes the line-of-sight requirement and enables the ingredient-based range and duration above.
entries.duration: Willpower Bonus minutes or days (with ingredient)

entries.name: Glamour
entries.text:
CN: 4 Range: Touch Target: 1 adult Duration: Willpower Bonus hours

Make an adult target appear any age within the normal adult range.

entries.name: Haunting Horror
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: Willpower days

Haunt one location, such as a house or clearing. Entrants other than witches and their familiars gain +1 Fatigued Condition. Then, unless Challenging (+0 SL) Psychology is passed, gain another Fatigued Condition and 1 Broken Condition; these latter two can only be removed by leaving the location.

entries.name: Make Hale
entries.text:
CN: 4 Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Instant

Heal the target WPB Wounds and remove 1 Fatigued and 1 Stunned. With +3 SL, you may use a Range of Willpower Bonus yards instead.

entries.name: The Evil Eye
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: 10 yards (maximum) Target: 1 (maximum) Duration: Instant

Make eye contact and resolve Opposed Intimidate/Cool, adding your Casting Test SL to your result. Winning gives the target Fear 1 of you and 1 Fatigued, plus another 1 Fatigued per +3 SL of victory. Winning by 6+ SL also gives 1 Broken.

entries.name: Destroy Lesser Daemon
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: 1 Size (Average) or smaller Daemon Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

The Daemon opposes your Casting Test with Easy (+4 SL) Endurance. If you win, destroy it immediately and optionally increase one of your Characteristics by +10 for the duration.

entries.name: Detect Daemon
entries.text:
CN: 4 Range: Willpower yards Target: Special Duration: Instant

Automatically detect whether a manifested Daemon is in range, including one summoned, bound into an artefact or possessing someone.

entries.name: Manifest Lesser Daemon
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: Special Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Manifest a Lesser Daemon, such as a Bloodletter or Daemonette (page 349), and resolve Opposed Channelling (Dhar)/Cool against it. On success it obeys one command literally, then vanishes if it completes the command before the duration ends. On failure it attacks immediately.

entries.name: Octagram
entries.text:
CN: 10 Range: Touch Target: AoE (Intelligence Bonus yards across, maximum) Duration: Willpower minutes

Draw an octagram on the floor with unholy symbols. Creatures with Daemonic cannot enter or leave it.

entries.name: Raise Dead
entries.text:
CN: 7 Range: Willpower yards Target: AoE (Willpower Bonus yards) Duration: Until sunrise

Raise 1 + SL Skeletons (page 339) from bare earth at the Round’s end, placing them as you wish within the area. Each starts Prone, is fully controlled by you and follows simple orders. Each +2 SL may add 1 Skeleton. Your death or becoming Unconscious ends the Spell and collapses them.

entries.name: Reanimate
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: Willpower yards Target: AoE (Willpower Bonus yards) Duration: Until sunrise

Reanimate WPB + SL corpses as Zombies (page 340), or skeletons as Skeletons (page 339), within range. They begin Prone, are fully controlled by you and obey simple orders. Each +2 SL may reanimate an additional WPB + SL Skeletons or Zombies. If you die or become Unconscious, the Spell ends and they fall dead again.

entries.name: Screaming Skull
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: Willpower yards Target: Special Duration: Instant

Send a skull in a straight line for the full Spell range, following ground contours and passing through obstacles. It deals a Damage +WPB magic missile to targets without Undead. Anyone losing Wounds must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Psychology or gain 1 Broken Condition.

entries.name: Vanhel’s Call
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Willpower yards Target: Special Duration: Instant

Give Intelligence Bonus targets with Undead an immediate free Move or Action when cast; choose the same option for all. Each +2 SL may affect another Intelligence Bonus targets.

entries.name: Festering Inflammation
entries.text:
CN: 5 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: 1 Duration: Instant

Turn one of the target’s Wounds into a Festering Wound.

entries.name: Miasma of Pestilence
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: You Target: AoE (Willpower Bonus yards) Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Living creatures in the area must pass Hard (-2 SL) Endurance or suffer Nausea (page 182). Nurgle’s devotees and skaven plague monks are exempt.

entries.name: Stream of Corruption
entries.text:
CN: 9 Range: Special Target: Special Duration: Instant

Immediately make an Unopposed Acid- and Poison-type Breath attack (page 357), treated as a magic missile with Damage equal to your Toughness Bonus that ignores Armour Points. A victim losing more Wounds than its own TB must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance or contract Blood Rot (page 179).

entries.name: Acquiescence
entries.text:
CN: 5 Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

At each Round’s start, the target must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance or lose both its Move and Action.

entries.name: From Pain, Pleasure
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Touch Target: 1 Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Give the target Painless (page 360) for the duration. Whenever it suffers a Critical Wound, it must pass Average (+2 SL) Endurance or drop its weapons and stand Helpless.

entries.name: Phantasmagoria
entries.text:
CN: 8 Range: You Target: AoE (Willpower Bonus yards) Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

Grant yourself and all allies in the area Distracting (page 358) for the duration. Affected targets do not distract each other.

entries.name: Boon of Tzeentch
entries.text:
CN: 9 Range: You Target: You Duration: Intelligence Bonus days

Choose one Spell from any Lore; cast it as memorised for the duration, but do not write it in a grimoire. To channel for it, use Channelling (Dhar) or its appropriate Channelling Skill if you possess that Skill. A Miscast while casting the borrowed Spell removes Boon of Tzeentch from your mind and also from your grimoire if recorded there.

entries.name: Transformation of Tzeentch
entries.text:
CN: 12 Range: Willpower Bonus yards Target: 1 Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds

The target becomes Prone and Helpless for the duration. At each Round’s end it must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance or gain 1 Corruption Point.

entries.name: Treason of Tzeentch
entries.text:
CN: 6 Range: Willpower yards Target: AoE (Initiative Bonus yards) Duration: Intelligence Bonus Rounds

Give targets Animosity (Allies). Unless immune to that Psychology, they cannot transfer Advantage to allies; if they score a Critical while attacking, they must pass Hard (-2 SL) Cool or target their nearest ally.

entries.name: Repeater Pistol
entries.qualities: Pistol, Repeater 4, Dangerous, Reload 4, Blackpowder, Damaging

entries.name: Bolas
entries.qualities: Inflict (Entangled 35), Inflict (Prone), Undamaging; Entangled and Prone only on leg hits

entries.name: Ablaze
entries.text: At Round end, take 1d10 Damage plus 1 per additional Ablaze, reduced by TB and the AP of the least protected location. Reaching 0 Wounds causes a Body Critical Wound. Normally affects flammable creatures, although some magical/divine effects bypass this restriction. A successful Athletics Test removes 1 Ablaze plus 1 per SL beyond the first; the GM sets Difficulty for the circumstances.

entries.name: Besmirched
entries.text: While thoroughly fouled, suffer Disadvantage on every Fellowship Test until cleaned. This Condition does not stack.

entries.name: Bleeding
entries.text: At Round end, lose 1 Wound per Bleeding, ignoring TB/AP. At 0 Wounds, replace this loss with a Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance Test each Round end; failure causes Unconscious. If Unconscious, Bleeding and at 0 Wounds, also roll 1d10 each Round end: a result no higher than your Bleeding count kills you; 10 removes 1 Bleeding. You cannot awaken while any remain. Each recovered Wound removes 1 Bleeding. Challenging (+0 SL) Heal removes Intelligence Bonus + SL Bleeding. A Bandage removes 1 without a Test, costing an Action or accompanying a Heal Test even if that Test fails.

entries.name: Blinded
entries.text: Cannot perform tasks requiring sight, including reading and Ranged Attacks. Melee Attacks and other strongly sight-dependent Tests, such as Climb/Ride, have Disadvantage. Melee attackers gain Advantage unless also Blinded. Normally remove 1 Blinded at your Turn's end; poison/injury causes may last longer.

entries.name: Broken
entries.text: Use Move and Action to Flee until hidden from all enemies, then your Action may improve concealment. Tests unrelated to running/hiding suffer −1 SL. While Engaged, cannot rally. Otherwise, a successful Cool Test at Round end removes 1 Broken plus 1 per SL beyond the first. Spending a full Round hidden from every enemy also removes 1 Broken.

entries.name: Deafened
entries.text: Cannot hear or understand speech unless Lip Reading is usable. Every minute (6 Rounds), attempt Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance; success removes 1 Deafened plus 1 per SL beyond the first.

entries.name: Entangled
entries.text:
Cannot Move; movement-related actions, including Grappling, suffer −1 SL. Spend an Action on Opposed Strength against the restraint: winning removes 1 Entangled plus 1 per SL beyond the first. For restraints without Strength, use the material value below.

| Material | Strength |
| --- | --- |
| Wool | 10 |
| Twine | 25 |
| Rope | 45 |
| Manacles | 65 |
| Heavy Iron Chain | 105 |

entries.name: Fatigued
entries.text: All Tests suffer −1 SL. Rest, a Prayer or a Spell can remove Fatigued. Rest depends on the cause: hard labour, forced marches or poison normally require a night's sleep; strenuous fighting, Frenzy or Stunned may need only minutes. Fatigued from Overburdened, disease, exposure or another ongoing effect ends when its cause ends.

entries.name: Poisoned
entries.text: Suffer −1 SL to all Tests and lose 1 Wound at Round end, ignoring TB/AP. At 0 Wounds, healing is impossible until all Poisoned are removed. If Unconscious, Test Endurance every TB Rounds or die. At each Round's end, successful Endurance removes 1 Poisoned plus 1 per SL beyond the first. Successful Heal by you or another removes the same amount. Endurance is normally Challenging (+0 SL), but the poison/venom sets the applicable Endurance/Heal Difficulty. Removing the last Poisoned gives 1 Fatigued.

entries.name: Prone
entries.text: Your Move may only stand you up or crawl at half normal Walking pace in yards. Movement-related Tests have Disadvantage; melee attackers gain Advantage. Does not stack; standing removes Prone.

entries.name: Stunned
entries.text: Movement is halved and all Tests suffer −1 SL. At Round end, successful Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance removes 1 Stunned plus 1 per SL beyond the first. Removing the last gives 1 Fatigued if none is already present. More Stunned than TB makes you Unconscious.

entries.name: Surprised
entries.text: No Action or Move; cannot defend Opposed Tests. Melee attackers gain +2 SL. Does not stack. Ends at Round end or after the first attempt to attack you.

entries.name: Unconscious
entries.text: You are Helpless, unaware and unable to act. Does not stack; becoming Unconscious removes all Stunned. Ordinary sleep usually ends after a few hours and may be interrupted. If another Condition/circumstance caused it, awaken when that cause ends. Spending Fortune to remove Unconscious without fixing its cause makes you Unconscious again at Round end.

entries.name: Durable
entries.text: Withstand Damage equal to the Durable rating before suffering item-damage penalties. Against instant breakage, save on 1d10 of 9+; each further purchase improves the save by 1 (Durable 3 saves on 7+). Repeat purchases are allowed.

entries.name: Fine
entries.text: An indicator of craftsmanship and social standing. Repeat purchases increase how impressive the item appears.

entries.name: Lightweight
entries.text: Reduce the item's Encumbrance by 1.

entries.name: Practical
entries.text: A failed Test using the item gains +1 SL. On armour, reduce each wearing penalty by one level, such as −3 SL becoming −2 SL.

entries.name: Bulky
entries.text: Add 1 Encumbrance. Bulky armour/clothing still has Enc 1 when worn. This Flaw normally cannot apply to small trinkets.

entries.name: Shoddy
entries.text: Breaks on a failed Test using the item when the roll is a double. Shoddy armour breaks when a protected location sustains any Critical Hit.

entries.name: Ugly
entries.text: Draws unfavourable attention; relevant Fellowship Tests may suffer −1 SL.

entries.name: Unreliable
entries.text: A failed Test using the item suffers −1 SL. Double the wearing penalties of Unreliable armour.

entries.name: Blackpowder
entries.text: Anyone targeted must pass the printed Average (+20) Psychology Test or gain 1 Broken, even when the shot misses.

entries.name: Blast (Rating)
entries.text: Affects everyone in a Rating-yard diameter and normally cannot be Opposed. Inflicts Weapon Damage and its Conditions, without SL Damage. Damaging still permits Damage from the units die.

entries.name: Damaging
entries.text: On a successful hit, use the higher of SL or the units die for the attack's Damage contribution. Undamaging overrides Damaging if both would apply.

entries.name: Defensive
entries.text: Gain +1 SL to Melee Tests opposing incoming attacks. Benefit from only one Defensive Quality at a time. Unbalanced overrides Defensive.

entries.name: Fast
entries.text: Add 20 to combat initiative only when attacking with this weapon. Using it for two-weapon fighting removes Fast.

entries.name: Hack
entries.text: On a hit, damage a struck armour piece or shield by 1 before resolving Damage against the wearer.

entries.name: Impale
entries.text: Successful combat attack rolls that are doubles or divisible by 10 cause a Critical Hit. A ranged Impale Critical leaves its ammunition embedded: arrows/bolts need successful Challenging (+0 SL) Heal to remove; bullets require a surgeon (Surgery Talent). Each unremoved arrow or bullet prevents recovery of 1 Wound.

entries.name: Inflict (Condition)
entries.text: A hit applies the named Condition, using any listed Strength/Difficulty. While Entangling someone, the weapon cannot be used otherwise; you may release them whenever you choose.

entries.name: Magical
entries.text: Can harm targets immune to non-magical attacks.

entries.name: Parry
entries.text: Defending with this weapon ignores the usual −2 SL off-hand penalty. When dual wielding, if the first attack hits, a second attack made with the Parry weapon is Unopposed.

entries.name: Dangerous
entries.text: A failed Test containing a 9 on either die causes a Fumble.

entries.name: Imprecise
entries.text: Attacks with the weapon suffer −1 SL.

entries.name: Penetrating
entries.text: Bypass 2 AP.

entries.name: Pistol
entries.text: May attack in melee without range modifiers; the attack can be Opposed like a melee attack.

entries.name: Precise
entries.text: Successful attacks gain +1 SL. Imprecise overrides Precise if both would apply.

entries.name: Pummel
entries.text: A Head hit that deals Wounds equal to the target's TB gives it 1 Stunned.

entries.name: Reload (Rating)
entries.text: After firing, spend Rating Actions reloading before firing again. A Repeater with shots remaining needs 1 fewer reload Action.

entries.name: Repeater (Rating)
entries.text: Holds Rating shots and reloads automatically between shots. Once empty, complete the weapon's normal full reload.

entries.name: Trap Blade
entries.text: When defending against a bladed weapon, a Critical may trap the blade instead of causing a Critical Hit; you must be at least the opponent's Size. The opponent drops the trapped blade. With Disarm, spend the printed Advantage to catch it in a free hand. Optionally Test Very Hard (−30) Strength, adding your Melee Test's SL: success breaks the blade unless Unbreakable.

entries.name: Unbalanced
entries.text: Defending with this weapon suffers −1 SL.

entries.name: Unbreakable
entries.text: Under nearly all circumstances, resists breaking, corrosion and loss of its edge.

entries.name: Undamaging
entries.text: Double AP against the weapon. Successful combat hits have no automatic minimum 1 Wound. For any Critical Wound it causes, roll twice and use the lower result.

entries.name: Wrap
entries.text: Melee Tests opposing its attacks suffer −1 SL.

entries.name: Flexible
entries.text: May be layered under non-Flexible armour; both layers provide their benefits.

entries.name: Impenetrable
entries.text: Disregard Critical Hits generated by an odd to-hit roll, such as 11 or 33.

entries.name: Partial
entries.text: An even Hit Location roll bypasses this armour's AP.

entries.name: Shield
entries.text: When opposing with Dodge or Melee, gain +1 SL (not cumulative with Defensive) and apply shield AP if hit. A shield with at least 2 AP permits Dodge against ranged attacks at any range. Only one shield provides benefits. A strapped/slung shield protects Head, Body and off Arm only, while allowing a two-handed polearm; a buckler allows an Enc 0 weapon in the off hand. Attacking with a shield uses Improvised Weapon rules, Personal Reach and Defensive; it then stops providing shield benefits until your next turn begins.

entries.name: Weakpoints
entries.text: An Impale weapon's Critical Hit bypasses this armour's AP.

entries.name: Animosity (Target)
entries.text: Fellowship-based Tests with the target group have Disadvantage. On meeting them, pass Psychology or insult, denigrate or attack; after doing so, you can temporarily tolerate their presence. Fear/Terror takes precedence: you need not confront a target you fear.

entries.name: Fear (Rating)
entries.text: Against unfamiliar hostile Fear sources, make one Extended Psychology roll each Round, targeting accumulated SL equal to the highest Fear Rating present. Success overcomes every source of that Rating or lower. Known allies do not trigger the Test. While affected, gain no Momentum; the feared source's Melee Attacks against you have Advantage.

entries.name: Frenzy
entries.text: On your Turn, a successful Willpower Test enters Frenzy. Gain immunity to other Psychology, one extra Melee Attack as a Free Action each Round, and +1 Damage to all Melee Attacks. Move/Action may only advance the goal of reaching and attacking the nearest foe. Frenzy ends when nearby foes are bested, or you become Stunned/Unconscious; immediately gain 1 Fatigued.

entries.name: Hatred (Target)
entries.text: Social interaction with the target group is impossible. On meeting them, pass Psychology or attempt their destruction by the quickest, deadliest means. Slaying/driving them off restores control; otherwise, another Psychology Test may restrain you at each Round's end after the first. Whether controlled or not, gain +1 SL to Melee/Ranged against them and ignore their Intimidate/Fear, but not Terror.

entries.name: Terror (Rating)
entries.text: First encountering a non-allied Terror source requires Psychology, using the highest Rating present. Success prevents further Terror effects that encounter. Failure gives Broken equal to Rating plus 1 per negative SL beyond the first. After resolving the Test, the source also causes Fear at the same Rating.

entries.name: Afraid
entries.text: Make an Extended Psychology Test against the target’s Fear. Until accumulated SL equal or exceed its rating, gain no Momentum; its melee attacks against you have Advantage (p. 183).

entries.name: Amphibious
entries.text: Has Swim; +1 SL to Swim Tests. Full Movement in water.

entries.name: Animosity
entries.text: On encountering the listed target, make a Psychology Test. Failure: attack socially or physically as appropriate; +1 SL to Fellowship-based Tests to oppose or disparage them (p. 183).

entries.name: Belligerent
entries.text: Immune to Fear while possessing Momentum.

entries.name: Bestial
entries.text: No rational thought/language; defends only with Dodge. Shies from fire; fire Wounds inflict Broken. Flees after losing over half Wounds; enters Frenzy instead if cornered, protecting young or Territorial.

entries.name: Bite
entries.text: Lose Momentum for a Free Attack at Rating Damage (SB already included); uses WS/BS without spending the turn’s Action.

entries.name: Blessed
entries.text: Can enact the listed deity’s Blessings; Pray at Fellowship +10 (GM may increase).

entries.name: Bounce
entries.text: When Charging, Leaping or Sprinting, double Movement and leap over intervening terrain and creatures.

entries.name: Breath
entries.text: Magical ranged Free Attack: choose a visible creature within 20 + TB yards; it and every creature within SB yards of it oppose a single Ballistic Skill roll with their own Dodge Tests. Use BS 30 if the attacker has no BS. Losing targets suffer Rating Damage. Apply any listed Breath type: Acid — TB +4 Damage, and all weapons and armour carried by targets take 1 Damage. Cold — SB +2 Damage and a Fatigued Condition; affected weapons have Slow until that Condition ends. Electricity — SB +2 Damage, ignoring metal armour, and a Stunned Condition. Fire — SB +3 Damage and an Ablaze Condition. Poison — TB +2 Damage and a Poisoned Condition. Smoke — fills the area, blocks line of sight and causes Suffocation (p. 169) for TB Rounds. The attacker is immune to its own Breath.

entries.name: Champion
entries.text: Winning an Opposed Test while defending in melee deals Damage as if attacking.

entries.name: Chill Grasp
entries.text: Lose Momentum and use an Action: Opposed WS against Dodge or Melee. Win: target loses 1d10 + SL Wounds, ignoring TB and AP. Magical.

entries.name: Cold-blooded
entries.text: Advantage on Cool Tests. Surprised is not removed the first time it normally would be.

entries.name: Constrictor
entries.text: Every successful hit inflicts Entangled; may then initiate a Grapple (p. 167).

entries.name: Construct
entries.text: No Int, WP or Fel; never Tests them, except use T for required WP Tests. Use SB instead of WPB for Wounds. All attacks Magical. Without a controlling spellcaster, or without Territorial, wanders mindlessly.

entries.name: Corrosive Blood
entries.text: Whenever wounded, all Engaged targets take 1d10 Damage (one roll for all).

entries.name: Corruption
entries.text: A Corrupting Influence of the listed strength (p. 187).

entries.name: Daemonic
entries.text: No food, water or air; all attacks Magical. Non-Magical blow: 1d10, Rating+ ignores it and any Critical. Cannot ignore Magical blows this way. At 0 Wounds, returns to Chaos and leaves play.

entries.name: Dark Vision
entries.text: Sees in darkness as in daylight.

entries.name: Disease
entries.text: Carries the listed disease; others Test for Contraction as appropriate (p. 179). Whether the carrier suffers its effects is the GM’s choice.

entries.name: Distracting
entries.text: Living targets within TB yards suffer −2 SL to all Tests. Does not stack with other Distracting creatures.

entries.name: Ethereal
entries.text: Passes through solid objects. Only Magical attacks can harm it; all its attacks are Magical.

entries.name: Fear
entries.text: Extended Psychology Test. Until accumulated SL exceed Rating (default 1): no Momentum; attackers gain Advantage in melee (p. 183).

entries.name: Fly
entries.text: As its Move, fly up to Rating yards, ignoring intervening terrain, obstacles and creatures; may Charge. End landed or airborne; if starting a turn airborne, must Fly or fall (GM decides distance). Against it, measure horizontal range then increase one range step (Extreme becomes unreachable). While flying, −20 to its Ranged Attacks.

entries.name: Frenzy
entries.text: WP Test to enter: Free Attack each Round, +1 Damage, immune to Psychology. Only attack or move to attack nearest visible enemy; no fleeing/retreat. Ends with no visible enemies or if Stunned or Unconscious; then Fatigued.

entries.name: Ghostly Howl
entries.text: Once per turn, lose Momentum for a Magical Free Attack. Living hearers within Strength yards gain 3 Deafened and lose 1d10 Wounds ignoring TB/AP; Average (+2 SL) Cool or also Broken.

entries.name: Grim
entries.text: At the end of its turn, gains Momentum if it has none.

entries.name: Hatred
entries.text: On meeting target: Psychology Test; failure activates Hatred. Attack by fastest, deadliest means; +1 SL Melee/Ranged against them. Immune to their Intimidate/Fear, not Terror (p. 184).

entries.name: Horns
entries.text: When Charging into combat, may make a Free Attack at SB +4 Damage.

entries.name: Hungry
entries.text: After killing/incapacitating living prey or finding a fresh corpse: Average (+2 SL) Cool or feast; lose next Move and Action.

entries.name: Immune to Psychology
entries.text: Ignores Psychology rules (p. 183).

entries.name: Immunity
entries.text: Ignores all harm of the listed type, including Critical Wounds.

entries.name: Infected
entries.text: On causing a living opponent to lose Wounds: Easy (+4 SL) Endurance or contract a Festering Wound (p. 180).

entries.name: Infestation
entries.text: Opponents suffer −1 SL to hit it in melee.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries.text: Casting Tests for spells affecting it suffer −3 SL. Incompatible with Channelling or Arcane Magic, Bless, Chaos Magic, Invoke, Petty Magic and Witch! Talents (in either direction).

entries.name: Magical
entries.text: All attacks are Magical and can harm creatures vulnerable only to Magical attacks.

entries.name: Many Heads
entries.text: Head Criticals stun, kill or render unconscious only when all heads are disabled or similarly affected. With Bite, Horns or Tongue, make as many Free Attacks as healthy heads. With 2+ healthy heads, +2 SL to Perception.

entries.name: Mark of Chaos
entries.text: Khorne: Frenzy; Etiquette (Followers of Khorne). Animosity towards overt Slaanesh followers (reciprocal while Mark visible). Language (Magick)/Channelling: dispelling only. Career Talents at normal XP: Berserk Charge, Combat Aware, Combat Reflexes, Furious Assault, Implacable, Magic Resistance, Resistance (Magic), Resolute, Strike Mighty Blow, Warrior Born. Nurgle: +10 Toughness; Etiquette (Followers of Nurgle). Animosity towards overt Tzeentch followers; they reciprocate while the Mark is visible. Career purchases at normal XP: Frightening, Hardy, Implacable, Iron Jaw, Menacing, Resistance (Poison), Resistance (Disease), Robust, Tenacious, Very Resilient. Slaanesh: Fearless (Everything); Etiquette (Followers of Slaanesh). Animosity towards overt Khorne followers; they reciprocate while the Mark is visible. Career purchases at normal XP: Attractive, Blather, Careful Strike, Combat Master, Gregarious, Inspiring, Lightning Reflexes, Nimblefingered, Resistant (Poison), Sharp. Tzeentch: Roll 1d10/3 Mutations, rounding up, alternating Mental and Physical. Etiquette (Followers of Tzeentch). Animosity towards overt Nurgle followers; they reciprocate while the Mark is visible. Career purchases at normal XP: Aethyric Attunement, Arcane Magic (Any), Chaos Magic (Tzeentch), Fast Hands, Instinctive Diction, Magical Sense, Petty Magic, Second Sight, War Wizard, Witch!.

entries.name: Mental Corruption
entries.text: Roll on the Mental Corruption table (p. 189).

entries.name: Miracles
entries.text: Can enact the listed deity’s Miracles; Pray at Fellowship +10 (GM may increase).

entries.name: Mutation
entries.text: Roll on the Physical Corruption table (p. 189).

entries.name: Night Vision
entries.text: See clearly in natural darkness for 20 yards; extend the illumination distance of light sources by 20 yards.

entries.name: Painless
entries.text: Ignores non-amputation Critical Wound penalties; Conditions still apply.

entries.name: Petrifying Gaze
entries.text: Lose Momentum and an Action against one visible living target: Opposed BS/Initiative (spellcasters may defend with Language (Magick)). Win: 1 Stunned, +1 per SL after the first. Win by 6+ SL: permanently turn target to stone.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries.text: Round start: above 0 Wounds, heal 1d10; at 0, heal 1 on 1d10 of 8+. A roll of 10 fully heals one Critical and its penalties/Conditions. Cannot regenerate fire-caused Wounds/Criticals.

entries.name: Size
entries.text: Size determines Wounds, primary melee Damage and combat interactions. Small: Wounds 2 × TB; no added Damage; counts as 1 when outnumbered. Average: Wounds SB + 2 × TB + WPB; no added Damage; counts as 1. Large: Wounds (SB + 2 × TB + WPB) ×2; add SB Damage; counts as 2. Enormous: Wounds (SB + 2 × TB + WPB) ×4; add SB Damage; counts as 3. Monstrous: Wounds (SB + 2 × TB + WPB) ×8; add 2 × SB Damage; counts as 4. These Damage bonuses are already included in NPC profiles and do not apply to ranged or extra attacks. Tiny has no supplied Wounds formula, Damage modifier or outnumbering count; retain its baseline or set Wounds manually. Melee defence against a larger creature suffers −2 SL. Aggressive creatures cause Fear in smaller creatures. Creatures may leave melee with smaller opponents without Disengaging. In Opposed Strength or similar Tests, a creature at least 2 Size steps larger wins automatically; with a 1-step difference, the smaller creature must roll a Critical to compare SL normally, otherwise it loses. The outnumbering counts above apply only when determining whether the larger creature is outnumbered; it counts as 1 for its own outnumbering bonus. Against a smaller opponent, lose Momentum for one Stomp as a Free Attack using Melee (Brawling), with SB Damage. Each upward Size adjustment gives +10 Strength, +10 Toughness and −5 Agility; reverse these changes when shrinking. Ignore Size rules while Swarm applies (p. 362).

entries.name: Skittish
entries.text: Spectacular visible magic, thunderclaps or explosions inflict 3 Broken Conditions.

entries.name: Spellcaster
entries.text: Casts the listed Lore(s). Add Spellcaster/Spellcaster Lord template, or grant Channelling (chosen Wind) at WP +10 and Language (Magick) at Int +10 as Basic Skills (GM may increase).

entries.name: Sprinter
entries.text: Run Movement ×1.5 when Running.

entries.name: Stealthy
entries.text: Stealth (Rural) at Agility +10 (GM may increase).

entries.name: Striding Gait
entries.text: No movement penalties in the listed terrain; +1 SL to Athletics and Stealth there.

entries.name: Stupid
entries.text: If no nearby ally lacks Stupid, make Easy (+4 SL) Intelligence at each Round’s start. Failure: lose that turn’s Move and Action. Nearby non-Stupid allies prevent this.

entries.name: Swarm
entries.text: Acts as one creature; ignores Psychology, Engaged restrictions on moving and all Size rules. Each Engaged opponent loses 1 Wound at Round end. Has ×5 normal Wounds and +10 WS; shooting at it gains +40 to hit.

entries.name: Tail
entries.text: Lose Momentum for a Free Attack at SB +2 Damage; smaller targets losing any Wounds also become Prone.

entries.name: Tentacles
entries.text: One Free Attack per tentacle at SB +0 Damage. Causing Damage may inflict Entangled and initiate a Grapple with that tentacle. Resolve its Grapple with the tentacle’s Free Attack, not the creature’s Action (p. 167).

entries.name: Territorial
entries.text: Fights to the death defending its area; normally does not pursue enemies beyond it.

entries.name: Terror
entries.text: First encounter: Psychology Test; failure gives Broken equal to Rating +1 per negative SL. Causes Fear of same Rating regardless of result (p. 183).

entries.name: Tongue
entries.text: Lose Momentum for a ranged Free Attack at SB +0 Damage. GM sets range (default 3 yards at Small–Large; 12 for larger). Hit: 1 Entangled; smaller targets dragged into melee. Then release, make a Weapon-Trait Free Attack, or keep wrapped and initiate a Grapple (p. 167).

entries.name: Tracker
entries.text: Track at Intelligence +10 (GM may increase).

entries.name: Trained
entries.text: Animal Training teaches the options listed in parentheses; additional training options may be created. Broken: ignore Bestial and gain +2d10 Fellowship. Drive: pull carts, coaches, ploughs, buggies or similar loads. Entertain: +10 to appropriate Entertain, Perform or Play Tests. Fetch: retrieve objects, normally for dogs and similar animals. Guard: remain at or patrol a guarded place; gain Territorial. Home: return home when released or lost. Magic: ignore Skittish caused by magic, as required for most spellcasters’ mounts. Mount: accept a rider; belligerent animals may require a specific Ride specialisation, such as Ride (Griffon) for a griffon. War: +10 Weapon Skill and ignore Skittish caused by loud noises.

entries.name: Undead
entries.text: Needs no air, food, water or other life necessities; counts as Undead for spells, Miracles and abilities.

entries.name: Unstable
entries.text: Round end: Engaged opponent has Momentum and creature has none → driven back; lose 2 Wounds. Destroyed or banished at 0 Wounds.

entries.name: Vampiric
entries.text: Successful Bite against suitable prey: heal Wounds equal to target’s loss. Blood-drinking is its only healing method.

entries.name: Venom
entries.text: Causing Wounds inflicts Poisoned. The listed Difficulty applies to Tests to recover from Poisoned, not to avoid it (p. 186).

entries.name: Vomit
entries.text: If starting the turn Engaged, spend Move and Action: one BS roll opposed by each target’s Dodge within 2 yards. Attacker Easy (+4 SL), defenders Challenging (+0 SL). Losing targets take TB +4 Damage and Stunned; all their carried weapons/armour take 1 Damage. Once per 12 hours.

entries.name: Wallcrawler
entries.text: Full Movement on suitable vertical surfaces and ceilings; automatically passes Climb Tests.

entries.name: Ward
entries.text: After any blow, roll 1d10: Rating+ ignores the blow, including Criticals.

entries.name: Web
entries.text: Each successful hit inflicts 1 Entangled, with Strength equal to Rating (p. 186).

entries.text:

| Silver | 10 silver shillings plus 1d10 per Standing Level |
| Gold | 2 gold crowns plus 1 per Standing Level |

Keep duplicate starting items as spares; they may be sold. Examples: Brass 3 gives 6d10+20 brass pennies; Silver 3 gives 3d10+10 silver shillings; Gold 3 gives 5 gold crowns. Spend or save this money; Chapter 11 gives items and coin values.

entries.name: Common Forms Of Skullduggery
entries.text:
| Action | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Pick a pocket | Sleight of Hand opposed by the target’s Perception. |
| Force open a door or window | Strength for speed; with suitable tools, Stealth (Urban) for silence. |
| Pick a lock | Pick Lock; lock quality sets Difficulty. Harder locks may require Extended Tests once per round or minute. |
| Connect with local criminals | Difficult (-1 SL) Gossip; Criminal grants Advantage. |
| Argue your innocence | Charm opposed by Cool, or opposed Lore (Law) in court. Disadvantage if caught in the act or incriminating evidence exists. |
| Cheat at cards | Sleight of Hand opposed by Perception; success grants Advantage to your next Gamble Test in that game. |
| Bribe a guard | Bribery identifies a willing recipient and Status-based price; Haggle may reduce it. |
| Learn a thing’s value | Evaluate for value; Difficult (-1 SL) Evaluate to identify a room’s most valuable object quickly. |

entries.name: Example Difficulties Of Common Underhanded Tasks
entries.text:
| Difficulty | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Very Easy (+6 SL) | Sleight of Hand: take bread from a helpless child. Charm: persuade an already furious mob to burn an object. Bribe: locate a corrupt dockside tax inspector in Übersreik. |
| Easy (+4 SL) | Stealth (Urban): disappear into a crowded night street. Lore (Law): establish that suspicion alone does not justify arrest. Intimidate: deter a common thief with superior arms. |
| Average (+2 SL) | Sleight of Hand: perform a familiar shell-game scam. Perception: notice an ogre on a nearby street. Gossip: identify a wealthy potential victim. |
| Challenging (+0 SL) | Gamble: win a few shillings from bored merchants. Charm: recruit thieves to teach you. Stealth (Rural): enter a noble’s manor unseen. |
| Difficult (-1 SL) | Evaluate: distinguish an authentic masterpiece among forgeries. Intimidate: demand protection money from a dwarf. Charm: persuade an angry mob to burn a person. |
| Hard (-2 SL) | Lore (Law): make a Witch Hunter honour a Wizard’s Licence. Gossip: circulate a false story about a famous knight’s wooden leg. Charm: sell a merchant a bridge fraudulently. |
| Very Hard (-3 SL) | Intimidate: drive a Shallyan away from her patient. Bribe: corrupt a Reiksguard Captain. Charm: persuade an angry mob to listen calmly. |

entries.name: Selection of Traps
entries.text:

entries.name: Trap Spot Difficulty
entries.text:
| Set Trap Result | Perception Test Difficulty |
| --- | --- |
| Astounding Success (+5 or more SL) | Very Hard (−3 SL) |
| Impressive Success (+3 to +4 SL) | Hard (−2 SL) |
| Success (+1 to +2 SL) | Difficult (−1 SL) |
| Marginal Success (+0 SL) | Challenging (+0 SL) |

Use Challenging (+0 SL) when Difficulty is unspecified or the setter is unknown or long gone. Obvious traps or those in barren, open areas with little concealment may require Average (+2 SL) Perception or easier.

entries.name: Common Social Tests
entries.text:
| Action | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Befriend a useful contact | Charm to build rapport or learn preferences; success may reveal information or grant Advantage to a later Test. |
| Make someone Fear you | Intimidate opposed by the target’s Cool. |
| Carouse with some soldiers | Perform, Play or Entertain for songs, music or stories; Consume Alcohol to join drinking. |
| Convince someone to do what you want | Charm opposed by Cool. Suitable Lore may replace Charm in intellectual debate. Intimidate can compel short-term compliance with later repercussions. |
| Talk your way in to a gathering | Charm opposed by Cool; appearance and the credibility of your explanation affect Difficulty. |
| Inspire a crowd | Charm opposed by the audience’s lowest Cool. Leadership works in military settings or where you hold authority. |
| Read the Room | Intuition to assess mood, leadership, followers and fears. |
| Lying | Cool, Charm or Entertain (Acting), opposed by the listener’s Intuition. |
| Spread a Nasty Rumour | Gossip; plausibility and supporting evidence determine Difficulty. |
| Negotiate a Discount | Haggle for a better price. |

entries.name: Example Difficulties Of Common Social Actions
entries.text:
| Difficulty | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Very Easy (+6 SL) | Charm: tempt a habitual gambler into one more double-or-nothing hand. Entertain (Singing): lead a tavern in a favourite bawdy song. Consume Alcohol: socialise with soldiers returning from patrol. |
| Easy (+4 SL) | Charm: befriend a hungry student over a meal you bought. Intimidate: deter a cowardly noble from a duel. Play (Lute): perform well enough for modest brass earnings. |
| Average (+2 SL) | Charm: avoid an underpaid guard’s search. Intuition: recognise a dubious business proposition as fraud. Leadership: organise disciplined troops to march. |
| Challenging (+0 SL) | Charm: spend a day begging for a few brass pennies. Intimidate: deter a petty thief. Gossip: circulate a merchant’s supposed bankruptcy. |
| Difficult (-1 SL) | Leadership: hold troops against cavalry. Charm: obtain a hearing from an enemy soldier before an attack. Consume Alcohol: keep pace with a dwarf. |
| Hard (-2 SL) | Perform (Juggling): entertain a ruthless noble under threat of a sword. Haggle: obtain a blacksmith’s discount before a siege. Intimidate: persuade an ogre of your toughness. |
| Very Hard (-3 SL) | Play (Bagpipe): impress Altdorf’s court memorably. Charm: stop a courtier disparaging you after you leave. Intuition: read a reserved dwarf longbeard. |

entries.text:
| 1d10 | Outcome |

| 1–2 | ‘Marienburger’s Courage!’: +2 SL to resist Fear. |
| 3–4 | ‘You’re My Besht Mate!’: Ignore existing Animosities (page 183). |

entries.name: Common Means Of Investigation And Research
entries.text:
| Action | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Tell how an animal died | Average (+2 SL) Animal Care; Challenging (+0 SL) for subtle poison or illness. |
| Tell a lie, or spot one | Charm opposed by Intuition; an implausible lie can increase Difficulty. |
| Ask around about someone | Gossip reveals opinions, with better results finding more secret or relevant details. Bribery identifies willingness to accept a bribe and a possible price. |
| Wring a secret from someone | Charm or Intimidate opposed by Cool; sensitivity of the information sets Difficulty. |
| Search a room or a crime scene | Perception reveals hidden details, with better results adding information. Disturbance increases Difficulty. |
| Extract information from books | Research identifies relevant libraries or books, or finds pertinent facts within them. |
| Recall a useful fact | An Advance in the appropriate Lore supplies basic facts; only obscure or unusual information needs a Test. |
| Spot a forgery | Evaluate, with Difficulty based on craftsmanship. |
| Follow someone’s trail | Track, with Difficulty based on conditions and trail age; oppose the quarry’s Track only if they concealed the trail. |

entries.name: Example Difficulties Of Common Investigative Tasks
entries.text:
| Difficulty | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Very Easy (+6 SL) | Gossip: identify the town’s most disliked person. Track: follow a wounded fawn through woods. Charm: persuade a drunk friend you will repay tomorrow. |
| Easy (+4 SL) | Evaluate: identify a misspelt property deed as forged. Research: recall that baronial deeds sit in the graf’s vault. Intimidate: obtain an accomplice’s name from a cowardly thief. |
| Average (+2 SL) | Track: follow a bandit across soft ground. Lore (Magic): recall the eight Winds’ colours and properties. Lore (History): recall Sigmar’s general life story. |
| Challenging (+0 SL) | Bribery: judge whether a guard will free a thief for payment. Charm: convincingly claim a different Imperial origin. Track: follow a fresh field or woodland trail. |

| Hard (-2 SL) | Research: find a daemon’s true name in a deranged wizard’s grimoire. Lore (Law): recall a decisive precedent. Track: follow a day-old trail over bare rocky mountains. |
| Very Hard (-3 SL) | Research: uncover a dwarf grudge’s full basis. Perception: notice one missing book on a huge shelf. Lore (Reikland): name every cousin of Karl Franz. |

entries.name: Common Lore Specialisations
entries.text:
| Specialisation | Information Provided |
| --- | --- |
| Engineering | Simple machinery, artisan identification and complex machines’ operating principles. |
| Geology | Stone identification, promising well or mine sites, and flood or collapse risks in caves. |
| Heraldry | Noble and military insignia, including coat-of-arms symbolism. |
| History | Relevant historical facts. |
| Law | Legal rules, loopholes, arguments and weaknesses in arguments. |
| Magic | Winds and their effects, magical traditions’ equipment, and whether a grimoire holds real spells. |

| Science | Natural phenomena and theories for unusual compounds, including black powder and soap. |
| Theology | Beliefs and practices of religions familiar to your culture, including Imperial or elven gods. |

entries.text:

entries.text:

| Hard (-2 SL) | Ride (Demigryph): charge into spears. Drive: stop a damaged cart before a ditch. Row: escape a hungry stirpike. |
| Very Hard (-3 SL) | Ride (Horse): jump a broken bridge. Climb: ascend smooth mountain granite in rain. Swim: survive a waterfall descent unharmed. |

entries.text:
After failed Ranged (Throwing), roll 1d10; T marks the target.

entries.name: Regional Events Table
entries.text:
The GM rolls one Regional Event for downtime, or substitutes an important local event, festival, misfortune or rumour relevant to a future adventure.

01–02: Grand Procession — The GM chooses the honoured Imperial god. Followers may make one Test with Advantage during the next adventure.

03–04: Unusual Mercenaries — Training or Unusual Learning with the visiting mercenaries reduces martial Skill or Talent training costs by 20%.

05–07: Auguries of the West Wind — Azyr Casting and Channelling gain +1 SL throughout the next adventure.

08–12: Teacher, Teacher! — The GM chooses an Advanced Skill; this downtime, Training can teach it without Consult an Expert to locate a tutor.

13–16: The Doktor is In — Improve Scarce and Rare Herbs and Draughts Availability one step this downtime (page 314). The visitor offers free amputations, extractions and haircuts.

17–21: Artisan Caravan — All Crafting Endeavour Tests gain +2 SL this downtime.

22–26: Flowing Profit — Riverfolk Income Endeavours earn 50% more this downtime.

27–30: Opportunity Saunters Through — Burgher and Peasant Income Endeavours earn 50% more this downtime.

31–35: Festivities — This downtime, Gossip has Advantage; Artists and Entertainers double Income Endeavour earnings.

36–39: Marvellous Miracle Cures — Improve Scarce and Rare Herbs and Draughts Availability one step when buying from the visitor this downtime (page 314). For each purchase the GM rolls d10: 1 or 2 replaces it with a GM-chosen Poison (page 313).

40–42: Levy — Warrior Income Endeavours earn 50% more and also count as Combat Training.

43–45: Travelling Players — Consult an Expert, Foment Dissent and The Latest News each cost one additional Endeavour this downtime.

46–52: Inclement Weather — During the next adventure, social Skill Tests suffer -1 SL and food costs 50% more.

53–55: Religious Mania — Pray Tests have Advantage this downtime.

56–59: Power Vacuum — Foment Dissent costs 1 Endeavour rather than 2 this downtime.

60–64: New Moon — Rogue Income Endeavours earn 50% more this downtime.

65–68: False Silver — Banking loses 20% of deposits; Income earnings also fall by 20%.

69–73: Tax Collector — Legal employment Income earnings fall by 50%; Rogues and other illegal workers earn twice normal Income.

74–81: Crime Crackdown — Rogue Income earns nothing. Rogues using Banking may choose only high-risk deposits.

82–88: Glorious Weather — During the next adventure, social Skill Tests suffer -1 SL; improve all non-Exotic goods’ Availability one step.

89–91: Local Crop Failure — Peasants cannot take Income; local food prices double for the next adventure.

92–94: Malicious Malady — Each Character passes Easy (+4 SL) Endurance or contracts Bloody Flux (page 180).

95–97: Riots — Courtiers cannot take Income. Foment Dissent Tests have Advantage.

98–00: Under Suspicion — Each Character loses one Endeavour hiding or proving innocence to the magistrate. Rogues cannot take Income until after their next adventure.

entries.name: Character Events Table
entries.text:
Each player rolls d100 for a downtime Character Event; effects may alter Endeavours or the next adventure.

01–04: Inspiration Strikes — Gain 50 XP.

05–09: Unexpected Esteem — Receive a reward appropriate to a previous good deed, available at the next adventure’s start. The GM determines the gift and may attach a complication.

10–14: Somebody Else’s Problem — Gain 1 additional Endeavour this downtime.

15–19: A Quiet Week — Ignore the first Fumble or Minor Miscast suffered during the next adventure.

20–24: A Good Day’s Work — For Income this downtime, increase Standing by 3 when determining earnings.

25–26: Is that an Original von Klapper? — Immediately sell one GM-chosen Trapping to a collector for twice its listed value, if desired.

27–29: Morr’s Embrace — Receive an inheritance before Endeavours: Brass, 20 brass pennies; Silver, 10 silver shillings; Gold, 2 gold crowns. Spend or bank it before the next adventure under Money to Burn.

30–34: Forewarned is Forearmed — Increase maximum Fortune by 1 for the next adventure.

35–41: What a Bargain! — Buy one Trapping at half its usual price.

42–47: Pedlar — Pay 6 d for ale to take Latest News without spending an Endeavour.

48–51: A Useful Connection — Take Commission or Research Lore without spending an Endeavour; associated Tests have Advantage.

52–56: Soothsayer — Pay 1 shilling to gain Doomed if absent, or replace an existing Dooming with a new page 118 roll. The fortune-teller cannot be found again for companions’ readings.

57–59: Arcane Auction — Buy a book for 2 GC. It may contain GM-determined secrets; you or a chosen literate Character may also take Research Lore without spending an Endeavour, with Advantage on required Tests.

60–67: Oi! You spilled my pint! — The GM chooses an offended faction; social Tests with its members have Disadvantage during the next adventure.

68–74: Onerous Obligations — Lose 1 Endeavour this downtime.

75–79: Impounded — Spend 1 Endeavour recovering a GM-chosen Trapping, or start the next adventure without it.

80–84: Ranald’s Wrath — Reduce maximum Fortune by 1 during the next adventure.

85–90: Scandalous Rumours — Fortune cannot be spent on social Tests during the next adventure.

91–92: Betrayed! — Agree a betrayer and motive with the GM. They or their agents may obstruct you at least once next adventure; the GM decides whether reconciliation is possible.

93–97: Accused Ally — The GM chooses an ally accused of a crime. A Law Guild Licence holder may spend 1 Endeavour and pass Average (+2 SL) Lore (Law) to defend them; otherwise the party spends 3 Endeavours to secure acquittal or an alibi. A freed ally owes a Major Favour (page 200). Otherwise the GM assigns punishment, potentially execution.

98–00: They’re a Witch! — Spend 1 Endeavour and pass Difficult (-1 SL) Charm to clear your name. Failure or inaction attracts a witch hunter, who may interrupt adventures until you are cleared. Killing them confirms suspicion and draws their allies.

entries.name: Advance Career
entries.text: After acquiring the required Trappings, Talents and Advances, spend this Endeavour and 100 XP to gain the next Career level. Fill 10 tracker boxes for level two, 12 additional boxes for level three and 14 additional boxes for level four.

entries.name: Animal Training
entries.text: Train one of your animals with an Average (+2 SL) Animal Training Test. On success, add one skill from the Trained Creature Trait (page 363) to that animal.

entries.name: Endeavours
entries.text:
While not adventuring, choose one Endeavour per week, up to three per downtime period. The GM decides availability according to location and circumstances. Career or Species obligations may use some of these Endeavours.

### Elves and Yenlui

An elf spends one Endeavour maintaining spiritual balance. This requirement does not apply when using the High Elf Player’s Guide’s detailed yenlui rules.

### Burdens of Power

At your Career’s highest level, skipping Income still requires its Earning Test. Success preserves Standing but earns no money; failure permanently reduces Standing by 1 within your Status Tier. Each later Income Endeavour restores 1 Standing, up to the current Career level’s maximum.

If this loss would reduce Standing to 0, drop from Career level four to level three at no XP cost, using its lower Status and future earnings. Keep all acquired Advances. Returning to the higher level requires paying its XP cost again.

entries.name: Banking
entries.text:
Money left after Between Adventures is lost before the next adventure unless saved through Banking. Choose one option.

### Invest with Banking House

Silver or Gold Status only. Choose a number from 1–10, or roll 1d10: this is both the percentage interest and the risk. Withdrawing requires another Banking Endeavour, immediately or after later adventures. Roll 1d100: at or below the risk, lose the entire deposit; above it, receive the original funds plus accrued interest.

### Stash the Loot

Available to any Status: hide the money or leave it with someone. Withdraw before an adventure without spending an Endeavour. Roll 1d100: on 10 or less, lose the entire stash; otherwise recover the original funds. Successful withdrawals from either option are available at the next adventure’s start, alongside Income earnings.

entries.name: Change Career
entries.text: Agree the new Career’s introductions, costs, permits and feasibility with the GM; Species restrictions still apply. Spend this Endeavour and 100 XP to change within your Class, or 200 XP to enter another Class.

entries.name: Combat Training
entries.text: Gain one reroll for a Melee or Ranged Skill Test during the next adventure. This Endeavour can be taken repeatedly.

entries.name: Commission
entries.text:
Commission one Exotic or bespoke Trapping per Endeavour. Find a capable craftsperson or supplier first, using Consult an Expert if necessary. Place the order and pay the item’s cost; collect after the next adventure. Each additional item needs another Commission Endeavour.

### Custom Gear

With GM permission, use two or more consecutive Commission Endeavours for more unusual items. These can be extremely expensive and may also require Favours or an adventure to obtain materials; no fixed additional price is supplied.

entries.name: Consult an Expert
entries.text:
Consult an expert to support another Endeavour or obtain knowledge. If none is known, make Challenging (+0 SL) Gossip: success finds a genuine specialist; failure finds a self-proclaimed authority whose advice the GM determines. The GM sets any payment or Favours; the different repayment rules for Favours are on page 200. Advice depends on the expert’s field, experience, biases and your questions.

When seeking knowledge rather than supporting another Endeavour, also record an Expert Reroll: use it once on a directly related Test before the next adventure ends.

entries.name: Crafting
entries.text:
Make a Consumer Guide Trapping, or another GM-approved item, with the appropriate Trade Skill, Trade Tools, raw materials and workshop. Materials normally cost one quarter of the item’s list price.

Make an Extended Trade Test. The GM sets its Difficulty, normally guided by Availability:

| Availability | Difficulty |
| --- | --- |
| Common | Average (+2 SL) |
| Scarce | Challenging (+0 SL) |
| Rare | Difficult (-1 SL) |
| Exotic | Very Hard (-3 SL) |

The GM also sets the target SL using the item’s listed price as a guide:

| List Price | SL |
| --- | --- |
| Brass | 5 |
| Silver | 10 |
| Gold | 15+ |

Each Flaw halves the required SL. Then add +5 SL for each Quality. Each Crafting Endeavour permits one roll towards the Extended Test. Keep unfinished work at your lodgings or carry it while adventuring if possible.

entries.name: Foment Dissent
entries.text:
Spend two Endeavours to build unrest against a person, group or institution; Agitators also count this as Income. Pass Average (+2 SL) Gossip, then Charm with Difficulty based on the target’s popularity. A hated noble may be Easy (+4 SL); a respected Shallyan hospice may be Hard (-2 SL). Failure of either Test ends the attempt.

Success allows a Charm Test next adventure to assemble a hostile crowd, at GM-set Difficulty. Success produces harassment and threats; Impressive or Astounding Success may trigger rioting or attempted burning. Failure produces no action; a severe failure may warn the target or allies. After successful dissent, redirecting the crowd during that adventure requires Charm two Difficulty steps harder.

entries.name: Earned Income
entries.text:
| Status Tier | Income |
| --- | --- |
| Brass | 2d10 brass pennies per Standing Level |
| Silver | 1d10 silver shillings per Standing Level |
| Gold | 1 gold crown per Standing Level |

If the Earning Test fails, roll normal earnings then halve them, rounding down. Events may modify income. Receive it after disposing of the previous adventure’s unspent money under Money to Burn. Example: a Brass 3 Prowler rolls 6d10; a failed Average (+2 SL) Stealth (Urban) Test halves 34 to 17 brass pennies.

entries.name: Income
entries.text:
Make an Average (+2 SL) Test with the Earning Skill printed in bold italics at your Career’s first level. Use the Status of your current Career level to determine earnings:

| Status Tier | Income |
| --- | --- |
| Brass | 2d10 brass pennies per Standing Level |
| Silver | 1d10 silver shillings per Standing Level |
| Gold | 1 gold crown per Standing Level |

On failure, roll normal earnings and halve the result, rounding down. Character Events may modify income. Receive this money after the previous adventure’s unspent money is lost.

### Without Income

If you skip Income during downtime, earn nothing and begin the next adventure with one coin for your Status Tier: 1 brass penny, 1 silver shilling or 1 gold crown. At your Career’s highest level, the Burdens of Power restrictions in the Endeavours overview (page 196) also apply.

entries.name: Invent!
entries.text:
Combine the properties of two or more existing Trappings into a new invention. The GM decides its effects and capabilities.

### Plan

Spend one Endeavour on blueprints and make a Trade (Engineer) Test at a GM-set Difficulty based on the invention’s ambition. Success completes the plans; each SL provides +1 SL when building it.

### Build

Use either Crafting or Commission:

- Crafting: You need the Skills required for every component. The Crafting Test is Very Hard (-3 SL), modified by the Plan bonus. Materials cost twice the components’ combined listed price and have the rarest component’s Availability.
- Commission: Find a suitable engineer, using Consult an Expert if necessary. Resolve Commission normally, except the cost is six times the components’ combined listed price.

entries.name: Research Lore
entries.text: Requires a suitable library, archive, guild record, temple or other knowledge source. Make Average (+2 SL) Research. Success reveals one useful, interesting or hidden fact about the chosen subject, plus one relevant fact per SL. Impressive or Astounding Failure supplies convincing false information. The GM may roll secretly.

entries.name: The Latest News
entries.text: Make Challenging (+0 SL) Gossip for news from elsewhere. Success gives an interesting rumour; SL sets detail and accuracy, and the GM chooses its subject. Impressive Failure supplies convincing false information. The GM may roll secretly.

entries.name: Raise Reputation
entries.text: Spend coin equal to your maximum Earnings (page 199): for example, earnings of 4d10 brass pennies require spending 40 brass pennies. Increase Standing by +1 until the next downtime, unless your reputation is damaged during the adventure.

entries.name: Study a Mark
entries.text: Observe a chosen criminal target and make Challenging (+0 SL) Perception, adjusted for the mark’s accessibility. On success, you may gain Advantage on one Test concerning that mark during the next adventure; record it. The GM also supplies information or misinformation according to SL. This Endeavour may be taken repeatedly.

entries.name: Training
entries.text: Train a Skill or Characteristic outside your Career by paying normal XP plus a tutor fee. For Basic Skills and Characteristics, pay pennies equal to XP; Advanced Skills cost twice that fee (page 191). Specialists may require Consult an Expert to locate a tutor. Some Lores require appropriate institutions; forbidden subjects may require an adventure to find a willing teacher, usually at greater cost and often a Significant Favour (page 200).

entries.name: Unusual Learning
entries.text: Learn the first level of an out-of-Career Talent; this cannot increase an existing Talent. Locate a suitable tutor, using Consult an Expert for obscure Talents or remote locations if needed. Training costs 4d10 silver shillings.

entries.name: Wrath of the Gods Table
entries.text:
Roll on a Pray Fumble or when its units die is at or below current Sin Points; the GM may also roll or choose a result for insulting a god. Add +10 per Sin Point, apply the result, then reduce Sin by 1, minimum 0.

| d100 | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 01–05 | Holy Visions: Fail Average (+2 SL) Cool and gain one Stunned; the GM describes the visions. |
| 06–10 | Think Over Your Deeds: For one week, successful Pray is capped at +0 SL. |
| 11–15 | Heed My Lessons: Pray suffers -1 SL for 1d10 + Sin Points Rounds. |
| 16–20 | Prove Your Devotion: Gain Prone until successful Average (+2 SL) Pray. |
| 21–25 | You Try My Patience: No Pray Tests for 1d10 Rounds. |
| 26–30 | You Do Not Understand My Intent: All GM-chosen deity-associated Skills suffer -1 SL for 1d10 + Sin Points hours. |
| 31–35 | Your Lack of Faith is a Sorrow to Me: No Pray Tests for 1d10 + Sin points Rounds. |
| 36–40 | Share My Pain: Lose 1 + Sin Points Wounds ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points; fail Average (+2 SL) Endurance and also gain one Stunned. |
| 41–45 | Your Cause Is Unworthy: Allied targets gain Prone. The deity’s Blessings and Miracles targeting them fail for 1d10 + Sin Points days. |
| 46–50 | Cease Your Prattling: No Pray Tests for 2d10 + Sin points Rounds. |
| 51–55 | Feel My Wrath: Lose 1d10 + Sin Points Wounds; fail Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance and also gain one Stunned. |
| 56–60 | I Shall Not Aid You: One GM-chosen deity-associated Skill suffers -1 SL for 1d10 + Sin Points days. |
| 61–65 | Divine Wounds: Gain 1 + Sin Points Bleeding. |
| 66–70 | Struck Blind: Gain Prone and 3 Blinded. Only successful Challenging (+0 SL) Pray removes these Blinded, at 1 + SL per success. |
| 71–75 | What Will You Sacrifice?: Lose 1d10 + Sin Points Wounds ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points; fail Difficult (-1 SL) Endurance and also gain one Stunned. |
| 76–80 | You Have Sinned Against Me: Use each Action for Pray for 1d10 + Sin Points Rounds. |
| 81–87 | Purge the Flesh: Lose 2d10 + Sin Points Wounds ignoring Toughness Bonus and Armour Points. Fail Hard (-2 SL) Endurance and gain one Stunned plus one per -1 SL. |
| 88 | Daemonic Interference: A Lesser Daemon appears within 2d10 yards and attacks the nearest target. |
| 89–95 | Fear My Wrath: Gain 1 + Sin Points Broken. |
| 96–100 | Go On Penance: Undertake a Penance. |
| 101–105 | Castigation: Reduce Wounds to 0 if higher; gain Unconscious until at least 1 Wound is restored. |
| 106–110 | Do Not Use My Name in Vain: Lose Bless and Invoke for 1d10 + Sin Points days. |
| 111–115 | Rely Not upon Your Vanities: Lose all Trappings; each completed Penance returns one taken magical item, if any. |
| 116–120 | You Abuse My Mercy: Lose Bless and Invoke for 2d10 + Sin Points days. |
| 121–125 | Behold Your Wickedness: Next normal Fortune refresh restores only 1 point. |
| 126–130 | Thunderbolts and Lightning: Reduce Wounds to 0 if higher; gain Ablaze. |
| 131–135 | Suffer as I Suffer: Gain 1 + Sin Points Bleeding each morning until completing a Penance. |
| 136–140 | Excommunication: Lose Bless and Invoke. First Penance restores Bless; second restores Invoke. Fellow cultists know; interactions are Very Hard (-3 SL), with no positive Difficulty adjustment. |
| 141–145 | Prove Your Worth: A Divine Servant appears within 1d100 yards and acts according to the god’s nature, potentially attacking, intervening or rebuking. |
| 146–150 | I Cast You Out: Permanently lose Bless, Invoke and all Pray Advances. Fellow cultists know; interactions are Very Hard (-3 SL), with no positive Difficulty adjustment. |
| 151+ | Called to Account: Summoned before the god; return requires spending a Fate Point. Return occurs at the GM’s chosen time and also applies I Cast You Out. |

entries.name: Travelling By Road
entries.text:
| d10 | Encounter |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Roadside Shrine: A shrine to Rhya, Taal or another god bears recent offerings. |
| 2 | Toll Gate: Two wardens collect tolls; one sleeps as the other argues over a farmer’s pigs. |
| 3 | Funeral Procession: A Morr priest leads mourners behind a shrouded corpse on a cart with a caged raven. |
| 4 | Gibbet: An old skeleton hangs beside a fresh warning against a crime. |
| 5 | Fellow Travellers: Roll Fellow Travellers for other road users. |
| 6 | Roadside Inn: A small coaching inn offers food and drink. |
| 7 | Beastman Totem: Bones, antlers and hides surround a marked tree with fresh blood beneath. |
| 8 | Marching Troops: Reikland pikemen pass; their officer orders you aside. |
| 9 | Corpse: An arrow-struck body lies ignored in the road. |
| 0 | Pyre: A body was burned at a roadside stake, then its forehead marked with a hammer or comet. |

entries.name: Travelling By River
entries.text:
| d10 | Encounter |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Drowned Tree: A dead river tree bears offerings and Manann’s trident. |
| 2 | Ferry Crossing: People, livestock and priests crowd a ferry despite the ferryman’s assurances. |
| 3 | Dead Man’s Boat: An empty bloodstained rowboat drifts with a trailing rope. |
| 4 | Fisherman’s Catch: A fisherman cuts an alarming catch loose. |
| 5 | Fellow Travellers: Roll Fellow Travellers for other river users. |
| 6 | Plague Barge: A shuttered deserted boat sits at anchor behind white rope near a tended Shallyan shrine. |
| 7 | Waterborne Revels: A drunken barge crew cheers a barrel falling overboard; its unattended helm still clears a bend. |
| 8 | Abandoned Camp: Two overturned boats lie beside slashed tents and scattered belongings; nobody alive is visible. |
| 9 | Warning Shot: An arrow from wooded banks hits the boat; possible goblins or a wood elf warning against landing. |
| 0 | Riverbank Gallows: Three fresh corpses hang beneath a death warning for piracy and smuggling. |

Apothecaries use ingredient-processing and measuring tools; carpenters use woodworking tools; engravers use cutting, marking and pressing equipment; smiths use metalworking tools and a forge.
