entries.name: Injuries
entries.text: Injuries are lasting effects of Critical Wounds and need specialist treatment or another stated remedy. The Critical Wound remains unhealed while its Injury persists.

entries.name: Broken Bone (Minor)
entries.text:
### Effects

The affected location cannot be used until healed. For an arm or leg, use the corresponding Lost Arm or Lost Leg rules. A head fracture requires a liquid diet and gives -3 SL to all Language Tests. A body fracture gives Disadvantage on Strength- and Agility-based Tests and halves Movement.

### Healing

Recovery takes 30 + 1d10 days. Then pass Average (+2 SL) Endurance to avoid lasting damage. Failure causes -1 SL to Agility Tests using an injured arm; permanent -1 Movement and -10 Agility for a body or leg fracture; or -1 SL to spoken Language Tests for a head fracture.

An Average (+2 SL) Heal Test within one week removes the need for that Endurance Test, provided the location remains bound and immobilised until healed. If the binding comes undone, another Average (+2 SL) Heal Test within a day is required to retain that benefit.

entries.name: Broken Bone (Major)
entries.text:
### Effects

Use Broken Bone (Minor), including the unusable location and its location-specific effects.

### Healing

Recovery takes 10 days longer than Broken Bone (Minor). All associated Tests are Challenging (+0 SL). A failed healing Test causes -2 SL to Agility Tests using an injured arm; permanent -2 Movement and -20 Agility for a body or leg fracture; or -2 SL to spoken Language Tests for a head fracture. The binding and early Heal rules of Broken Bone (Minor) still apply.

entries.name: Torn Muscle (Minor)
entries.text:
### Effects

Tests involving the injured location suffer -1 SL. A leg injury also halves Movement.

### Healing

The muscle partially heals after 30 - Toughness Bonus days. Successful Heal reduces this time once by 1 day, plus 1 further day per SL after the first.

entries.name: Torn Muscle (Major)
entries.text:
### Effects

Use Torn Muscle (Minor), but the penalty is -2 SL to all Tests. A leg injury also halves Movement.

### Healing

After 30 - Toughness Bonus days, the penalty for using the limb falls to -1 SL on relevant Tests. Complete healing takes another 30 - Toughness Bonus days. Heal can diagnose the damage but does not shorten recovery.

entries.name: Amputated Parts
entries.text:
When a Critical Wound specifies Amputation (Difficulty), pass Endurance at that Difficulty or gain Prone. Failure at -1 SL or worse also gives Stunned; at -4 SL or worse, gain Unconscious as well. All amputations need Surgery, and the associated Critical Wound remains unhealed until surgical treatment (p. 172).

The lasting effects are listed under Lost Arm, Lost Ear, Lost Eye, Lost Fingers, Lost Foot, Lost Hand, Lost Leg, Lost Nose, Lost Teeth, Lost Toes and Lost Tongue.

entries.name: Lost Arm
entries.text: Use Lost Hand, but a shield cannot be strapped to the missing arm.

entries.name: Lost Ear
entries.text: One lost ear has no measurable penalty. Losing both ears gives Disadvantage on hearing-based Perception Tests.

entries.name: Lost Eye
entries.text: If both eyes are lost, all sight-influenced Tests have Disadvantage, and opponents gain Advantage on melee Tests to hit you.

entries.name: Lost Fingers
entries.text: Each lost finger gives -1 SL to all Tests using that hand. Once four or more fingers on a hand are lost, use Lost Hand.

entries.name: Lost Foot
entries.text: Permanently halve Movement, rounding up, and lose 10 Weapon Skill and 10 Agility. Dodge and Athletics Tests have Disadvantage. Losing a second foot sets Movement to 1 and costs another 5 Weapon Skill and 5 Agility. Reduce the lost-foot Characteristic penalty by the number of toes previously lost from that foot.

entries.name: Lost Hand
entries.text: Tests normally needing two hands have Disadvantage, and two-handed weapons cannot be wielded. A shield can be strapped to the injured arm. If the primary hand is lost, off-hand weapon Melee Tests suffer -2 SL; reduce this penalty by 1 SL for each 100 XP spent relearning use of the other hand. Losing both hands requires prosthetics to manipulate objects.

entries.name: Lost Leg
entries.text: Use Lost Foot, and the Dodge Skill cannot be used at all.

entries.name: Lost Nose
entries.text: This always counts as an Impressive Scar, with +2 SL to Intimidate and -2 SL to Charm instead of the usual modifiers. Smell-based Tests have Disadvantage.

entries.name: Lost Teeth
entries.text: Every two lost teeth permanently reduce Fellowship by 1. Losing more than half the teeth (Humans: 16; Elves: 18; Halflings and Dwarfs: 20) doubles eating times and makes some foods almost impossible to eat.

entries.name: Lost Toes
entries.text: Each lost toe permanently reduces Weapon Skill and Agility by 1.

entries.name: Lost Tongue
entries.text: All Language Tests involving speech automatically fail. Communication must rely on other methods, such as sign language.

entries.name: Impressive Scars
entries.text: With enough visible scars, lost parts or other marks, and the GM’s agreement, gain permanent +1 SL to Intimidate Tests and -1 SL to Charm Tests.

entries.name: Black Plague
entries.text:
### Contraction

Test Average (+2 SL) Endurance for each hour or part-hour in an area with infected fleas, or when exposed to infected fluids. Previous survivors instead Test once daily with Advantage.

### Progression

Incubation: 1d10 hours
Duration: 3d10 days
Symptoms: Blight, Buboes, Fever

entries.name: Blood Rot
entries.text:
### Contraction

Develops from another disease or a Critical Wound.

### Progression

Incubation: Instant
Duration: 1d10 days
Symptoms: Blight, Fever, Malaise

entries.name: Bloody Flux
entries.text:
### Contraction

Fail Easy (+4 SL) Endurance after an infected source enters the mouth.

### Progression

Incubation: 1d10 hours
Duration: 1d10 days
Symptoms: Fever, Flux, Malaise

entries.name: Festering Wound
entries.text:
### Contraction

Fail Average (+2 SL) Endurance after fighting a creature with the Infected Trait. It can also develop from Infection.

### Progression

Incubation: 1d10 days; instant if it develops from another disease or Infection
Duration: 1d10 days
Symptoms: Fever, Malaise

entries.name: Galloping Trots
entries.text:
### Contraction

Fail Easy (+4 SL) Endurance after an infected source enters the mouth.

### Progression

Incubation: 1d10 hours
Duration: 1d10 days
Symptoms: Flux, Malaise, Nausea

entries.name: Itching Pox
entries.text:
### Contraction

Fail Average (+2 SL) Endurance after contact with an infected individual.

### Progression

Incubation: 1d10 days
Duration: 1d10 + 7 days
Symptoms: Pox

Permanent: Contracting Itching Pox makes you immune to catching it again.

entries.name: Packer’s Pox
entries.text:
### Contraction

Fail Easy (+4 SL) Endurance after contact with infected animals, hides or bodies.

### Progression

Incubation: 1d10 days
Duration: 5d10 days
Symptoms: Pox, Infection

entries.name: Ratte Fever
entries.text:
### Contraction

Fail Average (+2 SL) Endurance after combat in which infected rodents, including skaven with the Infected Trait, wounded you; or fail Easy (+4 SL) Endurance after an infected source enters your mouth.

### Progression

Incubation: 3d10 + 5 days
Duration: 3d10 + 10 days
Symptoms: Fever, Malaise, Pox

entries.name: Sea Sickness
entries.text:
### Contraction

Elves are immune. On a susceptible character’s first sea journey, fail Challenging (+0 SL) Endurance to become seasick. In rough weather, the Test is Average (+2 SL).

### Progression

Duration: For first-time seafarers, Test Average (+2 SL) Endurance after each day travelling at sea; success prevents this form of Sea Sickness permanently. For rough seas or other temporary causes, Test Average (+2 SL) Endurance hourly.
Symptoms: Nausea

entries.name: Weevil Cough
entries.text:
### Contraction

Fail Average (+2 SL) Endurance after contact with infected hay, wheat or flour, or when an infected person coughs nearby. Test about once per hour of exposure.

### Progression

Incubation: 1d10 days
Duration: 1d10 days
Symptoms: Coughs and Sneezes, Malaise

There is no reliable cure for Weevil Cough.

entries.name: Blight
entries.text: Test Average (+2 SL) Endurance daily, normally when sleeping. The first failure causes Unconscious, which cannot be removed while Blight persists. The second failure is fatal.

entries.name: Buboes
entries.text: All physical Tests suffer -1 SL; Fellowship Tests also suffer -1 SL if the swellings can be seen or smelled. A Heal Test by someone with Surgery can lance them and remove the penalty; failure causes a Festering Wound. Once lanced, Test Difficult (-1 SL) Endurance daily or the swellings return.

entries.name: Convulsions
entries.text: All physical Tests suffer -1 SL.

entries.name: Coughs and Sneezes
entries.text: At the start of a session, secretly roll 1d10: the GM may trigger the urge that many times at most during the session. Resist with Average (+2 SL) Endurance or spend your next Action coughing or sneezing. If not resisted, creatures within 3 yards are exposed and must Test for Contraction.

entries.name: Fever
entries.text: Agility, Dexterity and Psychology Tests suffer -2 SL.

entries.name: Flux
entries.text: Take opportunities for toilet breaks. Once per session, the GM can require an urgent visit: reach a suitable place within Toughness Bonus Rounds or gain Besmirched.

entries.name: Gangrene
entries.text: Roll percentile dice for a Hit Location (p. 164): Head affects the nose, Arm a finger, Leg a toe, and Body causes a Festering Wound. For an affected nose, finger or toe, Test Average (+2 SL) Endurance daily. Failure worsens it; after more failures than Toughness Bonus, that location loses all function and uses the Amputated Parts rules. While Gangrene persists, all Fellowship Tests suffer -1 SL.

entries.name: Infection
entries.text: Each Infection prevents recovery of 1 Wound. Test Very Easy (+6 SL) Endurance once daily or gain a Festering Wound. If you already have a Festering Wound, Test Easy (+4 SL) instead; failure causes Blood Rot. An Infection from lost Wounds ends when it causes a Festering Wound or receives treatment. A disease-caused Infection lasts until its disease is cured.

entries.name: Malaise
entries.text: Acute Sense Talents cannot be used. Language and Perception Tests suffer -2 SL.

entries.name: Nausea
entries.text: Whenever a Turn involves strenuous activity, such as running, climbing or fighting, Test Average (+2 SL) Endurance. Failure gives 1 Stunned and may cause Besmirched from vomiting; an empty stomach instead produces dry heaving.

entries.name: Pox
entries.text:
Fellowship Tests suffer -1 SL. Up to twice per session, the GM may trigger an urge to scratch. Resist with Average (+2 SL) Endurance; failure gives Fatigued, removable only by spending your next 1d10 Actions scratching.

When Pox ends, Test Average (+2 SL) Endurance. On failure, reverse those Test dice to find the Hit Location for permanent scarring (p. 164). A Head result permanently reduces Fellowship by 1.

entries.name: Disease and Infection
entries.text: Heal can diagnose a disease. The Test Difficulty depends on how rare it is and whether the diagnosing character has encountered it before.

entries.name: Disease Format
entries.text: Contraction explains how infection occurs. Incubation is the delay before Symptoms appear. Duration is how long untreated Symptoms last, after which the disease ends. Symptoms list its effects; Permanent lists lasting consequences when applicable.

entries.name: Treatment of Disease
entries.text: A carer needs at least one Heal Advance. Each day a patient rests under their care removes 1 additional day from the disease’s duration. Successful Challenging (+0 SL) Heal protects the carer from catching it that day; each SL after the first protects one other character. The GM may modify the Heal Test for the disease, conditions, supplies or stress.

entries.name: Cures and Tonics
entries.text: Pre-prepared cures usually require an Endurance Test at the Difficulty shown for that cure and Symptom in Effect Of Pre-Prepared Cures. Success suppresses the Symptom for 1 day. An Astounding Failure (-6 SL) causes Galloping Trots. See the Consumer Guide for purchasing medicines.

| Roll | Description | Wounds | Additional Effects |

| 01–03 | Dramatic Injury | T | Gain 1 Bleeding. After healing, the scar grants +1 SL to suitable social Tests; this benefit cannot be gained more than once. |
| 04–06 | Rattling Blow | 1 | Gain 1 Stunned. |
| 07–09 | Poked Eye | 1 | Gain 1 Blinded. |
| 10–15 | Ear Bash | 1 | Gain 1 Deafened. |
| 16–20 | Minor Cut | 1 | Gain 1 Bleeding. |
| 21–25 | Black Eye | 2 | Gain 2 Blinded. |
| 26–30 | Sliced Ear | 2 | Gain 2 Deafened and 1 Bleeding. |

| 36–40 | Fractured Jaw | 2 | Gain 2 Stunned and a Broken Bone (Minor). |
| 41–45 | Major Eye Wound | 3 | Gain 1 Bleeding and 1 Blinded; Medical Attention is required to remove this Blinded. |
| 46–50 | Major Ear Wound | 3 | Hearing Tests suffer –20. Receiving this result again permanently removes hearing. |
| 51–55 | Broken Nose | 3 | Gain 2 Bleeding; fail a Challenging (+0) Endurance Test and also gain 1 Stunned. |
| 56–60 | Broken Jaw | 3 | Gain 3 Stunned and a Broken Bone (Major); fail a Challenging (+0) Endurance Test and also gain Unconscious. |
| 61–65 | Mangled Ear | 4 | Gain 3 Deafened and 2 Bleeding; lose an ear, Amputation (Average). |
| 66–75 | Smashed Mouth | 4 | Gain 2 Bleeding; lose 1d10 teeth, Amputation (Easy). |
| 76–80 | Concussive Blow | 4 | Gain 1 Deafened, 2 Bleeding and 1d10 Stunned, plus 1 Fatigued lasting 1d10 days. |
| 81–85 | Devastated Eye | 5 | Gain 3 Blinded, 2 Bleeding and 1 Stunned; lose an eye, Amputation (Difficult). |
| 86–94 | Disfiguring Blow | 5 | Gain 3 Bleeding, 3 Blinded and 2 Stunned; lose an eye and nose, Amputation (Hard). |
| 95–99 | Mangled Jaw | 5 | Gain 4 Bleeding, 3 Stunned and a Broken Bone (Major); lose the tongue and 1d10 teeth, Amputation (Hard). |
| 00 or more | Shattered Skull | Death | The skull is destroyed; death is immediate. |

| Roll | Description | Wounds | Additional Effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01–10 | Jolted Wrist | T | Drop the item in the affected hand. |
| 11–20 | Jarred Arm | T | Drop the held item. Treat the hand as lost for 1d10 – Toughness Bonus Rounds, minimum 1 (Amputated Parts). |
| 21–25 | Minor Cut | 1 | Gain 1 Bleeding. |
| 26–40 | Sprain | 1 | Suffer a Torn Muscle (Minor). |
| 41–45 | Torn Muscles | 1 | Gain 1 Bleeding and a Torn Muscle (Minor). |
| 46–50 | Bleeding Hand | 1 | Gain 1 Bleeding. While this Bleeding remains, pass an Average (+20) Dexterity Test before any Action using an item in that hand, or drop it. |
| 51–55 | Wrenched Arm | 2 | Drop the held item; the arm is unusable for 1d10 Rounds (Amputated Parts). |
| 56–60 | Gaping Wound | 2 | Gain 2 Bleeding. Until Surgery closes the wound, each instance of Damage to this arm adds 1 Bleeding. |
| 61–75 | Clean Break | 2 | Drop the held item and suffer a Broken Bone (Minor). Fail a Difficult (–10) Endurance Test and gain 1 Stunned. |
| 76–80 | Ruptured Ligament | 2 | Drop held items and suffer a Torn Muscle (Major). |
| 81–85 | Deep Cut | 3 | Gain 2 Bleeding, 1 Stunned and a Torn Muscle (Minor). Fail a Hard (–20) Endurance Test and gain Unconscious. |
| 86–90 | Crushed Elbow | 3 | Drop the held item and suffer a Broken Bone (Major). |
| 91–95 | Damaged Artery | 3 | Gain 4 Bleeding. |
| 96–109 | Dislocated Shoulder | 4 | Treat the arm as lost (Amputated Parts). Gain 1 Stunned that lasts until Medical Attention. After that treatment, an Extended Average (+20) Heal Test with 6 SL resets the arm; arm-based Tests then suffer –10 for 1d10 days. |
| 110–115 | Severed Finger | 4 | Lose a finger, Amputation (Average), and gain 1 Bleeding. |
| 116–120 | Cleft Hand | 4 | Lose 1 finger, Amputation (Difficult), and gain 2 Bleeding and 1 Stunned. Each subsequent Round without Medical Attention costs another finger. Losing all fingers also loses the hand, Amputation (Difficult). |
| 121–125 | Mauled Bicep | 5 | Drop the held item; suffer a Torn Muscle (Major), 2 Bleeding and 1 Stunned. |
| 126–130 | Mangled Hand | 5 | Lose the hand, Amputation (Hard), and gain 2 Bleeding. Fail a Hard (–20) Endurance Test and gain Stunned and Prone. |
| 131–135 | Sliced Tendons | 5 | The arm is permanently unusable, Amputation (Very Hard). Gain 3 Bleeding and 1 Stunned; fail a Hard (–20) Endurance Test and gain Unconscious. |
| 136 or more | Brutal Dismemberment | Death | The arm is severed; shock and bleeding cause almost immediate death. |

Bandoleer: Carries roughly a dozen measured blackpowder charges to ease and speed handgun loading.

Slow Match: Sold by the yard; burns about 1 foot per hour.

Fuse: Sold by the yard; burns about 1 inch per second. Standard Quality has approximately a 5% failure chance over 10 yards; Shoddy fuse tests every 5 yards.

Bow String: Spare strings replace broken ones; higher Quality reduces breakage.

Whetstone: Enables blade sharpening. Sharpening services cost a couple of pennies per blade; the GM determines consequences of neglect.

Sealskin: Weatherproof coat; matching over-mittens prevent dextrous work. Good examples can help resist cold exposure (WFRP p. 181).

Silk Underwear: Reduces chafing.

Captain Braun’s Multi-Stove: Cooks several meals together, retains heat and uses less fuel with fewer visible signs of fire. May cook while moving but becomes hot.

Captain Braun’s Insta-Boiler: Enclosed cooker for faster cooking at lower heat; uses less fuel and is less conspicuous than an open fire. Can be used cautiously while moving.

entries.name: Slash (XA)
entries.text: Critical Damage also gives 1 Bleeding. Spend X Advantage to inflict one further Bleeding.

entries.name: Spread (Rating)
entries.text: Point Blank: one target and +Rating Damage. Short–Long: also hit the next Rating nearest visible creatures, with no pair more than Rating yards apart. Extreme: use the same multiple targets but reduce Damage by Rating.

entries.name: Trip
entries.text: After a hit, spend 2 Advantage for Opposed Strength/Athletics. Winning makes the opponent Prone; a mounted opponent first falls 2 yards. Losing adds nothing beyond normal consequences for losing an Opposed combat Test.

entries.name: Unbalanced
entries.text: Opposing an incoming attack with this weapon incurs −1 SL.

entries.name: The Shield Quality
entries.text: When opposing an attack with WS or Melee, add Shield Rating AP, including when the main-hand weapon defends and the shield is off-hand. No benefit when unable to Oppose, such as while Surprised. Rating 2+ also allows opposing missiles within line of sight. Ordinary off-hand penalties apply to that defence (printed −20); Melee (Parry) avoids them, and Defensive grants its +1 SL when applicable.

entries.name: Trained (Shock Cavalry)
entries.text: Requires Trained (War). A charging rider may pass through smaller creatures. entries.name: Structure Damage
entries.text:
Structure Toughness modifies incoming Damage; its Damage score measures what it can withstand. Wall statistics apply to a 5-yard section, so destruction of that section need not destroy the entire wall. Structures have no Hit Locations. When a ranged attack misses someone sheltered within or behind a structure, use the failed shot’s SL below to check whether it strikes the structure.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| LEVELS OF FAILURE | EFFECT |
| 0 to –2 | The shot hits the structure and can damage it. |
| –3 or lower | The shot also misses the structure. |

entries.name: Structure Critical Damage
entries.text:
| Roll | Description | Wounds | Additional Effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01–35 | Chipped | T | Randomly choose one Character on the structure or using it as cover. Debris deals Damage equal to the structure’s Toughness Bonus. |
| 36–50 | Jolted | 1 | Everyone on or inside must pass an Easy (+40) Athletics Test or gain Surprised. |
| 51–60 | Holed | 1 | A breach worsens cover; for example, Difficult (-10) Cover Penalty becomes Challenging (-0). |
| 61–70 | Rocked | 2 | Everyone on or inside must pass an Average (+20) Athletics Test or gain Prone. |
| 71–80 | Hail of Splinters | 2 | Debris hits everyone on the structure or using it as cover, dealing Damage equal to the structure’s Toughness Bonus. |
| 81–90 | Partial Collapse | 3 | Everyone on or inside must pass a Challenging (+0) Athletics Test or suffer a fall under the core rules. Halve the Encumbrance Limit. Artillery or other heavy equipment exceeding this new limit falls and cannot be used until repaired. |
| 91–95 | Breached | 3 | Debris deals Damage equal to the structure’s Toughness Bonus to everyone on or inside. Those Characters no longer receive cover from the structure. |
| 96 or more | Collapse | Destroyed | The structure is destroyed. Debris deals Damage equal to its Toughness Bonus to Characters using it as cover. Everyone on or inside tests for falling, then takes a weapon hit with Strength equal to the structure’s remaining Wounds. All artillery or other heavy equipment falls and cannot be used until repaired. |

entries.name: Crewed
entries.text:
Every crew member needs the relevant Ranged Skill; nominate one to make the firing Test. Extra crew do not improve weapon efficiency, but can help move it or replace casualties. Crew shortages impose cumulative penalties: short 1 doubles reload time, short 2 adds Imprecise, short 3 adds Dangerous. Each already-present Flaw instead adds printed −10 to firing Tests. One crew member may assist Tests for reload time. Misfires affect the entire crew.

| Crew | Crewed 2 Weapon | Crewed 3 Weapon | Crewed 4 Weapon |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | N/A | N/A | N/A |
| 3 | N/A | N/A | Double Reload Time |
| 2 | N/A | Double Reload Time | Gain Imprecise Flaw |
| 1 | Double Reload Time | Gain Imprecise Flaw | Gain Dangerous Flaw |

entries.name: Salvo
entries.text: Holds the listed Salvo number of shots; each firing reduces it by 1. Reload is unnecessary until Salvo reaches 0. May fire repeatedly in one Turn, with cumulative printed −10 to Ranged for each shot after the first; this sequence resets next Turn. On a misfire, resolve normal misfire effects and then the book's following table.

| 8–9 | For every remaining Salvo point, all crew take full Damage to randomly determined Hit Locations, using the units die as hit SL. Destroy the artillery. |
| 10 | Fire one shot per remaining Salvo point in a random direction, each travelling D100 yards. Anyone between the machine and an impact point must pass a Very Hard (-30) Dodge Test or be hit. |

entries.name: Simple vs Complex Pursuits
entries.text:
| Method | Simple pursuits | Complex pursuits |

| Fleeing | Start with 3 Distance if the opponent makes the free attack. If they forgo it to pursue, start with 1 Distance. | Determine initial Distance with the Athletics Test under Complex Pursuits: Test and Update Distance. Add +2 SL to this Test if the opponent made their free attack. |

entries.name: Benefits Of Advantage
entries.text:
Spend from the relevant Advantage Pool during a player’s or creature’s turn; consultation is not required.

| Advantage cost | Advantage spend | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Advantage | Batter | Special Action: Make an Opposed Strength Test. On a win, the opponent gains Prone and +1 Advantage. On a loss, the opponent gains +1 Advantage and your Action ends. Winning gives you no normal opposed-Test Advantage. |
| 1 Advantage | Trick | Special Action: Make an Opposed Agility Test. On a win, gain +1 Advantage and, if circumstances suit, inflict Ablaze, Blinded or Entangled on the opponent, choosing one. The GM may reject a Condition if you lack a suitable item or have already inflicted it on this opponent. On a loss, the opponent gains +1 Advantage and your Action ends. Winning gives no additional normal opposed-Test Advantage. |
| 2 Advantage | Additional Effort | Free Action: Before a Test, gain +10%; each further Advantage spent adds another +10% (3 Advantage gives +20%; 4 gives +30%). This Test cannot generate Advantage for you. |
| 2 Advantage | Flee from Harm | Move: Leave opponents without penalty; replaces Disengaging (WFRP p. 165). |
| 4 Advantage | Additional Action | Free Action: Take another Action, which cannot generate Advantage for you. This spend is limited to once per turn. |

Creature Traits may also be activated with the appropriate pool, following WFRP pp. 338–343.

entries.name: Initial Advantage
entries.text:
| CIRCUMSTANCES | ADVANTAGE AWARDED |
| --- | --- |
| Manoeuvrability: Superior movement, for example mounted troops or giant spiders among trees. | 2 |
| Outnumbering: More combatants, but fewer than twice the opposing number. | 1 |
| Outnumbering: A 2-to-1 numerical advantage. | 2 |
| Outnumbering: A 3-to-1 numerical advantage. | 3 |
| Surprise: An unexpected attack. | 2 |
| Terrain: Light cover or fortifications, or a favourable position such as a hill. | 1 |
| Terrain: Heavy cover or a key position such as a bridge. | 2 |
| Threat: A dangerous asset such as a warpfire thrower, Ogre or Troll. | 1 |
| Threat: An asset that can match several foes, such as an organ gun, Manticore or Griffon. | 3 |
| Threat: An asset that can match a dozen lesser foes, such as a Dragon or Greater Daemon. | 5 |

Example: Five adventurers surprise ten Goblins and a Shaman riding a Manticore. The allies gain 2 Advantage for surprise. Their opponents gain 2 for outnumbering them 2 to 1 and 3 for the Manticore, totalling 5.

entries.name: Fanmaris’s Perfect Shot
entries.text:
Warrior Endeavour: Pass a Difficult (–10) Ranged (Bow) Test after training to earn one Perfect Shot during the next adventure. Spend a combat Round aiming at an opponent, then declare the Perfect Shot and make a Ranged Test with all normal modifiers, including +20 for aiming. Apply every effect reached by the total SL; the effects are cumulative.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| SL | EFFECT (CUMULATIVE) |
| +1 | Choose the Hit Location. |
| +2–3 | Gain Penetrating for this attack (WFRP p. 298); if already present, add 2 Damage instead. |
| +4–5 | Inflict an automatic Critical Hit. |
| +6 | Gain Damaging for this attack (WFRP p. 297); if already present, gain Impact instead (p. 298). |

This Endeavour may be undertaken repeatedly.

entries.name: The Leitdorf Defence
entries.text: Warrior Endeavour: After undertaking it, pass a Difficult (–10) Melee Test to earn one use during the next adventure. After at least one Round engaged with an opponent, declare the Leitdorf Defence and attack with an Opposed Melee Test at –10. The defender cannot use Talents or Skill Advances against this attack. Resolve the attack, then: if you won, suffer 1d10 Damage ignoring Armour; if the opponent won, they inflict a Critical Hit.

entries.name: Warrior Endeavours
entries.text: Any Character can attempt Warrior Endeavours. If the Character has never belonged to the Warrior Class, increase the Difficulty of all related Tests by one level; Difficult (–10), for example, becomes Hard (–20).

entries.name: Alcatini Method
entries.text: Warrior Endeavour; requires at least two ranks of Drilled. After undertaking it, make a Difficult (–10) Leadership Test. Each SL lets one Character gain a rank of Drilled for the next adventure (WFRP p. 136). Those already possessing Drilled gain +1 rank, up to your own Drilled rank. Inspiring multiplies the number of recipients using its core table (WFRP p. 139): +3 SL and Inspiring 2 can grant +1 Drilled rank to 30 Characters.

entries.name: Count Punchausen’s Narrative Auction
entries.text: Warrior Endeavour: Sell an account of your adventures by passing a Difficult (–10) Charm Test or Challenging (+0) Entertain (Storytelling) Test. Success earns 2d10 shillings and, once during the next adventure, lets you reverse the dice of a Charm or Entertain (Storytelling) Test because a listener knows your published story.

entries.name: The Quartermaster Shuffle
entries.text:
Warrior Endeavour: Choose a Trapping and its desired Qualities. Round the final price up to whole Gold Crowns; the usual limit is 20 GC, which the GM may waive. Pass a Challenging (+0) Gossip Test to find an associate offering a job through which the item can be acquired as payment or during the job.

Then make a Difficult (–10) Melee or Ranged Test. Either result grants the item and a Critical Wound to a random Hit Location. On success apply –20 to Critical severity; on failure increase severity by the item’s price in Gold Crowns. Critical Deflection cannot negate this wound, though spending Fate may avert some consequences. The tables on p. 139 can generate the job.

entries.name: Beat Blade
entries.text: Max: Weapon Skill Bonus. Tests: Melee for Beat Blade. Declare Beat Blade before using your Action for a non-Opposed Melee Test. Success removes 1 Advantage from the opposing Pool; 6 SL removes one more. Requires an armed opponent no larger than you.

entries.name: Distract
entries.text: Max: Agility Bonus. Bonus Tests: Athletics to Distract. Spend your Move on an Opposed Athletics/Cool Test. If you win, the target cannot generate Advantage for its Pool until the next Round ends.

entries.name: Drilled
entries.text: Max: Weapon Skill Bonus. Bonus Tests: Melee beside an ally with Drilled. Count as two combatants when determining Losing Advantage (p. 137).

entries.name: Flee!
entries.text: Max: Agility Bonus. Tests: Athletics while fleeing or as pursuit Quarry. Count Movement as 1 higher in those circumstances.

entries.name: Gunner
entries.text: Max: Dexterity Bonus. Add Gunner level SL to Extended Tests to reload blackpowder weapons. In combat, reloading also counts as Assess, with +1 extra Advantage from that Assess Test.

entries.name: Rapid Reload
entries.text: Max: Dexterity Bonus. Add Rapid Reload level SL to Extended Tests to reload ranged weapons. In combat, reloading also counts as Assess, with +1 extra Advantage from that Assess Test.

entries.name: Relentless
entries.text: Max: 1. Flee from Harm costs only 1 Advantage.

entries.name: Reversal
entries.text: Max: Weapon Skill Bonus. Tests: defensive Melee. After winning an Opposed Melee Test, you may transfer 1 Advantage from the opposing Pool to yours instead of gaining +1 Advantage. This causes no Damage, including on your own Turn.

entries.name: Roughrider
entries.text: Max: Agility Bonus. Tests: Ride in combat. With Ride, direct your mount to take an Action as well as a Move without a Ride Test. While mounted, use the mount’s Size when resisting Fear or Terror caused solely by an enemy’s Size. This does not protect against other causes, such as Daemonic or Undead nature.

entries.name: Shieldsman
entries.text: Max: Strength Bonus. Tests: shield defence. Once per turn while defending with a Shield, spend 2 Advantage either to deal Damage as though attacking on your Action or to push the attacker 2 yards directly away and end engagement.

entries.name: Vice (Target)
entries.text: Max: Willpower Bonus. Tests: Willpower to resist the chosen Vice. Each purchase gives a different Vice, such as Alcohol, Food, Narcotics or Pleasure. Encountering its target requires a Psychology Test (WFRP p. 190). Failure forces unhealthy indulgence instead of all other actions or duties, until insensible; gain one Fatigued Condition. At each later Round’s end, another Psychology Test can end this state. Fellowship Tests towards witnesses suffer −20. Each full day without indulgence adds a cumulative −20 to Psychology Tests until you indulge.
entries.conversion: Printed Vice Psychology is reference text, not a campaign tracker or permanent Fellowship adjustment. Species grants Vice (Food). No old per-rank SL Talent bonus is imported.
entries.adaptation: Fourth Edition per-rank bonus on the listed Tests omitted; printed limit and effects retained under the approved Fifth Edition adaptation.

entries.name: Bonecrusher
entries.text: A Damage +4 magic missile ignores Armour Points but allows Toughness Bonus. If it causes a Critical Wound, add +20 to the severity roll on the relevant Critical Wound table. Casting requires chewing a mouthful of bones.
entries.conversion: Current core Creature Traits apply; old page references identify Fourth Edition. Numeric effect modifiers remain printed unless explicitly converted here.

entries.name: Bullgorger
entries.text: Consume a mighty beast’s heart to grant the target +2 Strength Bonus for Damage and other appropriate feats of Strength for the duration. When it ends, the target must immediately eat a substantial meal or gain a Fatigued Condition. An unwilling target can reject the effect with a Difficult (−1 SL) Cool Test.
entries.conversion: Current core Creature Traits apply; old page references identify Fourth Edition. Numeric effect modifiers remain printed unless explicitly converted here. User resolves conflicting Difficult (+20) by the difficulty label: Difficult (−1 SL).
entries.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

entries.name: Braingobbler
entries.text: After eating a whole head, including its brains, gain Fear 2 (WFRP p. 341). Anyone resisting this Fear who had a close relationship with the head’s former owner takes −20 on their Cool Tests.
entries.conversion: Current core Creature Traits apply; old page references identify Fourth Edition. Numeric effect modifiers remain printed unless explicitly converted here.

entries.name: Taste Death
entries.text: Eating part of a corpse reveals approximately when and how it died, including the general weapon or cause, but no further detail or culprit. A death free of poison or disease is considered clean; custom then calls for consuming the remaining corpse.
entries.conversion: Current core Creature Traits apply; old page references identify Fourth Edition. Numeric effect modifiers remain printed unless explicitly converted here.

entries.name: Trollguts
entries.text: Swallow a little Troll Bile or a similar substance to give the target Regeneration (WFRP p. 341). Ogres have no additional effect. Each non-Ogre who recovers Wounds this way must pass an Average (+2 SL) Endurance Test or develop mottled green or blue new flesh, especially on regrown limbs. This is not a mutation, though observers may mistake it for one.
entries.conversion: Current core Creature Traits apply; old page references identify Fourth Edition. Numeric effect modifiers remain printed unless explicitly converted here. Regenerate uses current core Regeneration (p. 360); Average (+20) difficulty uses +2 SL under Appendix I p. 364.
entries.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

entries.name: The Maw
entries.text: Consume most of a large beast to open a bottomless, toothed pit. Everyone in the area immediately Tests Challenging (+0 SL) Dodge. Success avoids falling but causes a Damage +8 hit, reduced by 1 per SL on that Test. Failure causes a Damage +10 hit to a random location and 3 Entangled Conditions, opposed by Strength 60; all 3 must be removed to escape. Each creature inside takes another Damage +10 hit to a random location at the end of each of its turns. When the spell ends, the pit disappears; anyone still inside suffers a Critical Wound to a random hit location.
entries.conversion: Current core Creature Traits apply; old page references identify Fourth Edition. Numeric effect modifiers remain printed unless explicitly converted here. Challenging (+0) difficulty uses +0 SL under Appendix I p. 364.
entries.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

entries.name: Feast of the Fallen
entries.text: Bathe a blade in a freshly slain foe’s blood. Chosen creatures in the area gain Vampiric (WFRP p. 343) for the duration, activating it by wounding enemies in melee without needing to bite; other healing still works. An unwilling creature can resist with a Difficult (−1 SL) Endurance Test. When the spell ends, non-Ogres who wounded an enemy in melee must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Cool or gain a Stunned Condition. If they wounded a creature with Infected or Diseased, Tests against those Traits’ harmful effects take −30.
entries.conversion: Current core Creature Traits apply; old page references identify Fourth Edition. Numeric effect modifiers remain printed unless explicitly converted here. User resolves conflicting Difficult (+20) by the difficulty label: Difficult (−1 SL). Challenging (+0) difficulty uses +0 SL under Appendix I p. 364.
entries.adaptation: Printed Test Difficulty modifiers converted to Fifth Edition SL modifiers (core Appendix I).

mechanics.gmApproval: No Ogre may take writing, complex-artistry or suitably advanced Lore Skills/Talents without GM permission (Archives II p. 21). Confirm with your GM which of your choices need permission and obtain it before finishing creation.

magicReferences.text: Use Toughness for Language (Magick). Casting requires suitable meat within living costs; without it, lose Wounds equal to the spell’s CN. Ordinary meat does not protect against Miscasts. Esoteric ingredients cost 1 shilling per CN or may be acquired. The page separately charges CN Wounds when casting without a suitable ingredient; the GM must adjudicate this wording. These references do not automatically deduct Wounds or coins.

After successfully casting a Great Maw Lore spell, roll 1d10. On 10 or a result equal to or above the unmodified CN, recover that many Wounds. Use the unmodified CN despite Channelling or a Grimoire. Ingredients include bloody animal parts, unusual bile, marrow and cured fat. Healing is a play reference and is not applied automatically.

Carrying capacity is doubled after core Talent effects. Use current core Size rules, not the old combat summary on p. 28.

entries.name: Identifying A Magical Artefact
entries.text:
Detect Artefact allows Intuition on touching the item (WFRP page 135). Other Wizards normally spend one week per attempt in a suitable laboratory, equipped library or ritual space, then make Challenging (+0) Lore (Magic).

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SL | Result | Consequences |
| +6 or more | Astounding Success | Identify the item and every Quirk. |
| +4 to +5 | Impressive Success | Identify the item and whether it has Quirks; the GM may conceal one Quirk’s details. |
| +2 to +3 | Success | Identify the item and visible Quirks, but no hidden ones. |
| +0 to +1 | Marginal Success | Identify the item and one hidden quirk. |
| 0 to -1 | Marginal Failure | Identification fails and is known to have failed. Clearly visible Quirks are recognised. |
| -2 to -3 | Failure | Misidentify it as a similar item; recognise clearly visible Quirks. |
| -4 to -5 | Impressive Failure | Misidentify it as a similar item; recognise clearly visible Quirks and wrongly infer one further Quirk. |
| -6 or less | Astounding Failure | Misidentify it as a similar item; recognise clearly visible Quirks and wrongly infer at least two further Quirks. |

entries.name: The Finished Result
entries.text:

| --- | --- | --- |
| SL | Result | Consequences |
| +6 or more | Astounding Success | The item gains Unbreakable. |
| +4 to +5 | Impressive Success | Create without complications; add one chosen Item Quality (WFRP page 292). |
| +2 to +3 | Success | Create without complications. |
| 0 to +1 | Marginal Success | Create without flaws, taking 50% longer. |
| 0 to -11 | Marginal Failure | Create with one Quirk or curse from page 56. Reroll no-effect or Dwarf-rune results with +40. |
| -2 to -3 | Failure | Roll two Quirks or Curses with +40; reroll no-effect and Dwarf-rune results. Also choose one Item Flaw (WFRP page 292). |
| -4 to -5 | Impressive Failure | The artefact is useless; restart creation. |
| -6 or less-6 or less | Astounding Failure | The artefact explodes, causing a Bomb-equivalent hit (WFRP page 295). |

entries.name: Battlefield Strength
entries.text:
Before battle, the GM assigns each Army Power from 0 to 100 based on relative size and strength. Use these comparisons as guidance.

entries.name: Battle Endeavours
entries.text: Between Adventures, Characters may undertake up to three pre-battle Endeavours within the time the GM allows. Resolve their Skill Tests directly or play scenes or adventures. Retry a failed Endeavour only with a different approach.

entries.name: Infiltrate
entries.text: Requires successful Scout. Make Combined Stealth and Perception, or Combined Entertain (Acting) and Perception to impersonate an enemy soldier; the GM sets Difficulty. Scout results may offer other approaches. Success grants +20 to Plan. Failure forces escape or capture. A different Species makes infiltration significantly harder.

entries.name: Inspiring Speech
entries.text: Test Leadership with Difficulty based on the Armies’ Power difference rounded to the nearest 10. Success grants +10 to the Army’s first Battle Round Power Test.

entries.name: Muster Forces
entries.text: Gather troops through payment, persuasion, bribery or intimidation; circumstances determine Skills and Difficulties. Success adds +5 Army Power; Astounding Success (+6) adds +10; Astounding Failure (−6) reduces Power by −10.

entries.name: Sabotage
entries.text: Requires successful Scout, whose findings determine sabotage options. Usually Test Stealth or Entertain (Acting), possibly during Infiltrate. Success reduces enemy Power by −5, or −10 on Astounding Success (+6). Failure requires fleeing or fighting out of camp.

entries.name: Scout
entries.text: Make Challenging (+0) Combined Ride and Perception. Success reveals enemy numbers, distance, troop types and Power, granting +10 to Plan. Failure gathers incorrect information or returns too late, giving no bonus. Astounding Failure (−6) may require escaping enemy scouts to avoid capture.

entries.text:

Traps inflict 8 Damage and appropriate Conditions: Entangled for bear traps or Prone in pits. Each activation lets nearby Characters attempt Hard (−20) Perception to avoid later traps. Capturing the enemy engineer’s trap plan neutralises all traps. |

| 4 | Corrupting Influence: At each Battle Round’s end, everyone passes Challenging (+0) Endurance or gains 1 Corruption. The GM may make Easy (+40) Endurance using average troop Willpower, typically 35. Failure makes a nearby ally mutate and attack either side. |
| 5 | Toxic Cloud: Obscures like fog. At each Combat Round’s end, occupants pass Challenging (+0) Endurance or gain Poisoned. Ignition inflicts 3 Ablaze Conditions on everyone inside. |
| 6 | Rough Undergrowth: Halve Movement; Fumbles also cause Entangled. A blade user may clear it in a Cinematic Scene with successful Melee. |
| 7 | River: Those smaller than Large suffer −20 Combat Tests. Ending a turn in the river requires Challenging (+0) Strength to avoid being swept away. Controlling the bridge makes only the enemy cross the river. |
| 8 | Inferno: Moving requires Challenging (+0) Athletics to avoid 1 Ablaze Condition. Disable its source to extinguish it after 1 Battle Round. |
| 9 | Undeath: Each Army Power lost gives the enemy +1 Power. Defeat the necromancer to end this and remove all Power gained this way. |
| 10 | Fear: Army Power Tests suffer −10 while the enemy’s terrifying structure stands. |

entries.name: New Endeavour: Recuperation
entries.text: Make Very Hard (–30) Cool, potentially easier with good care. Success removes one chosen Psychology. Whether successful or not, during the next adventure you may reverse one Cool Test resisting Psychology.

entries.name: A Deal’s a Deal
entries.text: After a successful Haggle Test, thank Handrich and shake hands to add +2 SL to that Test, increased by 1 per +2 SL on the Pray Test invoking this Miracle. The other negotiator also forms a favourable impression of you.
entries.conversion: Use Fifth Edition magic and core Traits/Talents. Valid old Test Difficulties use Appendix I SL modifiers; ordinary printed numeric bonuses remain reference text. Play effects are not automated.

entries.name: Carry My Burdens
entries.target: One non-monstrous creature (as determined by the GM)
entries.text: Once delivery of goods has been agreed, pass an Animal Training Test to make the target serve as your pack animal, regardless of its usual aggression or wildness. It carries whatever you require during the journey but neither attacks nor obeys other commands. It returns to its wild state on arrival. Only one creature can be affected at once.

entries.name: Shake On It
entries.text: Seal a deal with a handshake. The target cannot oppose its terms for at least Fellowship Bonus Rounds. To contest them, they must beat your SL on an Average (+2 SL) Cool Test; success permits refusing one required action, and each additional 2 SL permits one action against the deal. You sense any breach. Breaking it yourself while the Miracle lasts gives you +1 Sin point.

They can contest your SL with a Challenging (+0 SL) Fellowship Test: beating you preserves their point; beating you by +4 SL also lets them spend 1 of yours as their own. A transferred point must be spent before that session ends; it returns to its original owner at the next session’s start.

entries.name: Fellstave
entries.text: When learning this spell, choose Beastmen (including Minotaurs and Centigors, excluding Skaven), Daemons, Orcs and Goblins, Ogres, Fimir, Trolls, or Undead; the GM may allow other types. Each further purchase costs the normal new-spell XP and selects another type. Whittle a wooden post at least three feet long and four inches across, carve warding symbols, and drive it into the ground before casting. For one month, matching creatures within 100 yards must pass Challenging (+0 SL) Cool or gain a Broken Condition. After recovering, they Test Challenging (+0 SL) Intuition; success identifies the Fellstave as the source of their magical panic.

entries.name: Enterprise Events
entries.text:
Between adventures, an Enterprise investor may replace their normal Events roll (WFRP page 193) with this table before choosing Endeavours. Only one investor per Enterprise may do so in a downtime phase; an Enterprise receives at most one Event.

| d100 | Event | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 01–02 | Looming Bankruptcy | Lose the latest Expansion’s benefits but retain its increased Debt and Interest; repay all Debt to restore them. Without an Expansion, close the business, dismiss staff and sell Trappings; Debt remains. The GM may allow an adventure to avert failure. |
| 03–05 | Recession | No Character may use this Enterprise for Earning or Income Endeavours until the next adventure ends. |
| 06–08 | Shoplifter Strikes | The most valuable portable Trapping is stolen; recover it during the next adventure or accept the loss. |
| 09–10 | Interest Inflation | Double Interest Payments until all Debt is repaid. |
| 11–13 | Trapping Degrades | The GM degrades a Trapping: item Flaw, lost animal Trained Skill or employee Condition. Severe effects are usually temporary, milder ones persistent; an already degraded item may be destroyed or lost. |
| 14–16 | New Competition | Undertake at least one Income Endeavour with it in this batch, receiving only 50% of normal income. The rival remains an ongoing threat. |
| 17–20 | Forced to Diversify | The GM blocks the most-used Source of Income for this batch of Endeavours; other sources remain usable. |
| 21–23 | The Dreaded Auditors | Spend an Endeavour helping auditors or pay 10% of Start-Up Costs or latest Expansion Costs, whichever is higher. |
| 24–26 | Gimme a Discount | Decide whether to discount now; resolve consequences next adventure. Refusal causes public slander; acceptance may prompt other demands and reduce Income Statuses. |
| 27–30 | I Need a Holiday | You cannot choose Income in the next batch of Endeavours; other investors may still use the Enterprise for Income. |
| 31–33 | Conservative Investments | No Character can acquire an Expansion Creditor during the next batch of Endeavours. |
| 34–36 | The Grind | If possible, choose Income before the next adventure; no other effect. |
| 37–39 | I Quit! | An NPC employee, if present, leaves; replace them by the next adventure’s start. |
| 40–41 | New Creditor | The current Creditor transfers the Debt to a new Creditor. |
| 42–44 | Closed for Refurbishment | No Income from the Enterprise during the next batch. Afterwards improved accommodation may grant GM-chosen Skill Test bonuses. |
| 45–48 | Creditor Visits | Before the next adventure, repay Debt (page 8) without spending an Endeavour. |
| 49–51 | New Hire | Gain an NPC employee who requires substantial training and supervision. |
| 52–54 | Breakup Opportunity | If Expanded, you may surrender the latest Expansion’s Trappings and benefits to clear all Debt. Later Expansion remains possible. |
| 55–57 | Alternate Event 1 | Use the specific Enterprise template’s Alternate Event 1. |
| 58–60 | Alternate Event 2 | Use the specific Enterprise template’s Alternate Event 2. |
| 61–63 | Business as Usual | No special effect. |
| 64–66 | Co-Ownership | If accepted, the co-owner pays half the outstanding Debt; you must accommodate their development ideas. |
| 67–69 | Upgraded Trapping | The GM improves a Trapping: item Quality, animal Trained Skill, employee Skill, or appropriate removal of a Flaw or Condition. |
| 70–72 | Merger Opportunity | Investors may immediately Expand, paying normal costs but no Endeavour, even while indebted. Creditor funding adds to current Debt. Use the new Expanded Interest rate until all Debt is repaid. |
| 73–75 | Desperate Customer | Choose a Source of Income; increase its effective Status number by 1 until the next adventure starts. |
| 76–78 | In the Black | No additional effect. |
| 79–81 | Temporary Expansion | Gain the next Expansion level’s benefits until the next adventure ends, without Expansion Costs or changed Interest. |
| 82–85 | Taking Care of Itself | Immediately take an Income Endeavour with the Enterprise; it does not count against the pre-adventure maximum. |
| 86–88 | Innovation | Gain a Source of Income agreed with the GM, including required Trappings and effects. Usually match the second-highest existing effective Status and use a different Earning Skill. |
| 89–91 | Rolling Profits | Choose a Source of Income and permanently increase its effective Status number by 1. |
| 92–94 | New Trapping | Gain either a duplicate Trapping or a new one worth no more than Start-Up Costs or latest Expansion Costs, whichever is higher. |
| 95–97 | Unexpected Generosity | Skip this downtime’s Interest Payment. |
| 98–100 | Offer to Buy-Out | If all investors accept, surrender Enterprise benefits, clear Debt and split wealth equal to double Start-Up Costs or double latest Expansion Costs, whichever is higher. |

entries.name: Goodwill
entries.text: CN: 0 Range: You Target: AoE (Fellowship Bonus yards) Duration: Willpower Bonus Rounds. Fellowship Tests in the area gain +10. Animosity and Hatred have no effect there.

entries.name: Mirkride
entries.text: CN: 0 Range: You Target: You Duration: Willpower Bonus minutes. Your spirit enters the Hedge, retaining its Characteristics, Skills and Talents. It can see the physical world, pass non-magical barriers, and is invisible and silent to physical beings and immune to non-magical Damage. It cannot handle physical objects, but can cast spells affecting them. It can see and interact with invisible, spirit, ethereal and Daemonic creatures. Your body stays immobile, insensate and Prone. The spell’s end returns you to it; touching your body also ends the spell. If your body dies during the spell, your spirit wanders forever.

entries.name: Nepenthe
entries.text: CN: 0 Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: The drink lasts Willpower Bonus hours; its effects are permanent. You need a cup or other drinking vessel to collect the conjured silver liquid. Drinking it permanently erases everything the drinker knows about one individual they choose.

entries.name: Nostrum
entries.text: CN: 0 Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: Willpower Bonus hours. Enchant a prepared draught. Drinking it before the spell expires restores Wounds equal to your Willpower Bonus and cures one disease you choose, plus one further disease per +2 SL on the Casting Test.

entries.name: Part the Branches
entries.text: CN: 0 Range: You Target: You Duration: Willpower minutes. You can see invisible creatures, spirits and Daemons in the spirit world.

entries.name: Protective Charm
entries.text: CN: 0 Range: Touch Target: Special Duration: Willpower Bonus days. Enchant a small charm, such as jewellery or a pocket trinket. Its bearer gains Magic Resistance; an existing Magic Resistance Talent receives no benefit.

entries.name: Spirit-Bonding Ritual
entries.text: CN: 30 Type: Any Lore Learning XP: 150. Requires a magically gifted animal that has been broken or befriended through an Animal Training Endeavour and attuned to your spirit for at least 1 week. No sacrifice is required, but its death may cause trauma (Corruption & Death, p. 81). Failure removes the animal’s Trained (Magic) Trait. Repeating the ritual requires another week of attunement.

entries.name: Animal Telepathy
entries.text: Caster and spirit-bonded familiar may initiate silent, non-verbal communication within 4 yards. Complexity is limited by the animal's Intelligence.

entries.name: Invisibility
entries.text: Once daily, the familiar becomes nearly invisible for its Willpower in hours; this cannot end early. Spotting it requires Very Hard (−30) Perception. While it hides, only observers with Magical Sense can spot it.

entries.name: Messenger
entries.text: The familiar can carry messages up to its Intelligence in miles away, following complex instructions without an Intelligence Test even beyond 4 yards from its caster. Unexplored routes may cause delay or danger. Use a tied-on letter, or speech if it has the appropriate Language Skill.

entries.name: Sensory Sharing
entries.text: The caster uses the bonded familiar's sight, hearing and smell at a range in miles equal to the lower of their Willpower scores. This does not permit casting from the animal or extend Animal Telepathy beyond 4 yards.

Next round it is pulled towards you, suspended about 5 yards above and 2 yards in front of your head, moving with you until expiry. Each +1 SL adds one Entangled or lifts it another 2 yards, maximum 10 yards. Release causes falling damage (WFRP p. 166).

Targets on or beside it need Challenging (+0 SL) Dodge to avoid falling; Marginal Failure allows grabbing the edge. Horses and vehicles fall automatically, and structures may partly collapse. At expiry it closes, dealing 20 Damage to trapped victims and burying them alive with Suffocation (WFRP p. 181).

entries.name: Erect the Edifice
entries.text: Raise a wall from local earth and stone, 5 yards long, 1 yard high and 6 inches thick, providing Hard Cover (WFRP p. 161), or Earthwork under Up In Arms artillery rules. Each +2 SL allows an extra round adding 5 yards length or 1 yard height; each extra yard of height adds 6 inches thickness. Each 2-yard section may have one door/window opening. A bend or curve costs +2 SL. Repeated castings can make a building shell, but it collapses after Willpower Bonus + SL days unless you or an adviser present during casting have Lore (Engineering) or Trade (Stoneworker). The spell makes no basements, floors or roofs; finishing needs carpentry.

Each exterior wall of a small two-storey house is roughly 4 × 4 yards; full coverage may need repeated casting. Taking cover behind it reduces Corruption exposure by two levels and gives +1 SL to Dispel spells targeting you. It can contain Malignant Influences such as Warpstone.

Rivers generally know events within 1 mile upstream/downstream from the last 24 hours; forest trees have similar reach and years of memory, but take at least 5 minutes per answer. Complex questions may receive vague answers. Spirits may demand help, need not like you, and this grants no advantage communicating with animated spirits such as Naiads or Dryads.

entries.name: Brew Potion
entries.topic: Spellcasting, ritual magic and specialist magic
entries.text: As one Endeavour, brew one batch of a chosen potion using the process on p. 160. Have its ingredients ready or obtain them with Commission or Gather Ingredients. A laboratory is required unless you have Concoct (p. 161).

entries.name: Gather Ingredients
entries.topic: Spellcasting, ritual magic and specialist magic
entries.text: If the GM agrees a suitable ingredient-gathering location is close enough, spend one Endeavour gathering there under p. 155’s process, which normally takes a week. A failed attempt may be retried as a second Endeavour.

entries.name: Improve Familiar
entries.topic: Spellcasting, ritual magic and specialist magic
entries.text:
A familiar cannot use Endeavours independently. Its creator must take Improve Familiar and pass a Hard (–20) Research Test; the familiar may assist. Success lets the familiar immediately undertake one eligible Endeavour, which it must still complete normally:

- Training (WFRP p. 199).
- Unusual Learning (WFRP p. 199), excluding Bless, Invoke and Pure Soul.
- Train with Unusual Weapon (Altdorf p. 219), for Combat Familiars only.
- Test Magic Item (Altdorf p. 219), for Spell or Power Familiars only.

Each successful Improve Familiar grants one such opportunity.

entries.name: New Endeavours
entries.topic: Spellcasting, ritual magic and specialist magic
entries.text: Spellcasters may take these Endeavours between adventures. Magical-item crafting Endeavours are in Archives of the Empire vol II.

entries.name: Perform Ritual
entries.topic: Spellcasting, ritual magic and specialist magic
entries.text: A ritual may be performed between adventures as an Endeavour. With GM and Player agreement, the caster can locate a site with Heavy or Extreme magical Saturation. Halve the ritual’s CN, rounding up, to represent careful preparation and a slower pace; the required channelled energy is unchanged. Its effects may end before the next adventure, and enemies may learn of the ritual and prepare countermeasures.

entries.name: Randomly Generating New Careers
entries.topic: Spellcasting, ritual magic and specialist magic
entries.text:
When randomly generating a Career from WFRP pp. 30–31, use the second roll below if the initial Career has an alternative. The Player may keep the first Career instead of rolling again; a second roll may still return that Career. These Careers can also be entered later through the normal XP and circumstance requirements.

| Career | ACADEMICS |
| --- | --- |
| Apothecary | 01–75: Apothecary 76–00: Mundane Alchemist |
| Wizard | 01–95: Core Wizard or a College Career: Hierophant, Alchemist, Druid, Astromancer, Shadowmancer, Spiriter, Pyromancer or Shaman. 96–00: Magister Vigilant |

| 2 | Morr | Death, Dreams | Intuition. Reversed: Intuition. |
