entries.name: Mine Events
entries.text:
Roll for a mine event at each month’s end or during downtime.

| Roll | Event and effect |
| --- | --- |
| 01–50 | Quiet Month: normal operation. |
| 51–53 | Petering Out: Motherlode becomes Rich Vein, Rich Vein becomes Lucky Strike, Lucky Strike becomes Hardscrabble, or Hardscrabble ceases production. |
| 54–55 | New Find: an actively managing owner may pass Challenging (+0) Perception to discover another strike. Otherwise an employee claims it and becomes a competitor. |
| 56–65 | Flooding: without pumps, d10 miners must pass Challenging (+0) Swim or drown; work stops for two weeks. |
| 66–68 | Inspired Workforce: each miner produces 1 GC extra ore this month. |
| 69–74 | Attack!: fortification sends attackers elsewhere; otherwise lose 2d10 employees. With none left, the mine is captured. Paid-up guild membership provides help organising its recapture. |
| 75–78 | Legal Entanglements: an employed Lawyer or guild membership resolves the claim. Otherwise lose d10 months of output and hire a Lawyer in that time or pass Very Hard (−30) Charm to avoid losing the mine. |
| 79–83 | Labour Strike: guild members replace dissenters. Otherwise the owner or Foreman must pass Challenging (+0) Leadership or work stops until weekly pay increases by –/6. |
| 84–87 | Corruption: a random employee steals 2d10 shillings of ore weekly. At next month’s end, Hard (−20) Gossip identifies them; failure lets them flee with d10 GC of ore. |
| 88–90 | Bad Air: each miner must pass Difficult (−10) Endurance or succumb to gas; Caged Canaries improve this to Average (+20). |
| 91–94 | Suffocation: bellows prevent loss; otherwise lose d10 miners. |
| 95–97 | Cave In: the owner or employed Engineer tests Difficult (−10) Trade (Engineer). Success limits losses to one week’s excavation and shoring. Failure traps 2d10 miners, each needing Difficult (−10) Climb to survive. |
| 98–99 | Equipment Malfunction: a random piece fails. Owner or employed Engineer may pass Hard (−20) Trade (Engineer) for emergency repairs; failure requires a replacement. |
| 00 | New Seam: employ up to five additional miners. |

entries.name: Night Goblin Net
entries.text: Night Goblin net. Group: Night Goblins; Reach: SB × 2; Damage: —; Entangle (Strength 40).
entries.notes: Printed Night Goblins Group/Strength 40 Entangle profile is reference-only; it does not replace the existing core Net or invent a Ranged group, price or weight.

entries.name: Bribery for smuggled cargo
entries.text:
For smuggled cargo, consider honesty, risk and relevant Skills/Talents when setting Bribery Tests (WFRP p. 120). Without special circumstances, persuading authorities to overlook it is never easier than Challenging (+0).

| Difficulty | Modifier | Cargo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Challenging | 0 | Taxed ordinary goods: wool, cloth, leather, beer or paper. |
| Difficult | −10 | Luxuries: fine wines/spirits, quality cloth, silk, perfume or fancy feathers. |
| Hard | −20 | Banned ordinary goods: weapons, armour or intoxicants. |
| Very Hard | −30 | Treasonous/heretical cargo: anti-Sigmarite texts, necromantic ingredients, warpstone or forbidden books. |

entries.name: Smuggled Goods Generator
entries.text:
Roll d100.

| d100 | Goods | Cost Modifier | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01–60 | Taxed, Ordinary | 50% | Cloth, wool, preserved foods, metal ore. |
| 61–85 | Taxed, Luxury | 60% | Fine brandy/wine, quality cloth, silk, art. |
| 86–95 | Banned, Ordinary | 70% | Prohibited ordinary or luxury goods. |
| 96–99 | Banned, Special | 80% | Gunpowder, weapons, stolen unique luxuries, heresy or magic items. |
| 00 | Treason! | 90% | Necromancy, Daemonology, Chaos or threats to an Elector’s safety/rule. |

Taxed Ordinary, Taxed Luxury and Banned Ordinary sell at Consumer Guide list prices (WFRP p. 288). Cost Modifier gives the average discounted buying price for the goods’ tax/legal risk. The GM prices Banned Special and Treason! items. These are bargaining starting points: except for Treason!, a successful Opposed Challenging (+0) Haggle Test reduces price another 10%; failure leaves it unchanged. Bargain for Treason! goods through roleplay.

entries.name: Smuggling Events
entries.text:
A Smuggler taking Income during downtime also rolls d10 here alongside normal events. Resulting questions mainly provide flavour; the GM may develop them into adventures.

| d10 | Event and effect |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Ratted Out!: pass Hard (−20) Stealth or earn nothing. |
| 2 | Desperate Seller: may earn 50% extra from unusually cheap contraband. |
| 3 | Help! The Watch!: pass Hard (−20) Perception or stolen goods leave no income. |
| 4 | Flooded Market: may earn 50% less. |
| 5 | Lucky Find: gain d10 GC in addition to normal income. |
| 6 | New Partners: double income, but unless Difficult (−10) Charm succeeds, the local crime boss demands a 60% employer’s share. |
| 7 | It Must Be Mine!: pass Average (+20) Haggle to double income, or triple it with Dealmaker. |
| 8 | Switcheroo: pass Hard (−20) Evaluate or worthless/spoiled goods yield no income. |
| 9 | Market Day: roll Earnings twice and use the higher amount. |
| 10 | Corruption: earn nothing; pay d10 shillings in bribes or Income is unavailable until moving to another town/city. |

entries.name: Dislocated Knee
entries.text: Wounds: 4. Gain Prone; leg unusable until reset (Amputated Parts, page 177). Extended Average (+2 SL) Heal, 6 SL, one Test per Round, resets it. Then halve Movement for 1d10 days.

entries.name: Cracked Shin
entries.text: Wounds: 4. Gain 1 Stunned, Prone, Broken Bone (Minor) and Torn Muscle (Major).

entries.name: Broken Knee
entries.text: Wounds: 4. Gain 1 Bleeding, 1 Stunned, Prone and Broken Bone (Major).

entries.name: Crushed Foot
entries.text: Wounds: 4. Gain 2 Bleeding. Fail Average (+2 SL) Endurance and also gain Prone, losing 1 toe plus 1 per SL below 0, Amputation (Average +2 SL). Without Surgery within Toughness Bonus days, lose the foot.

entries.name: Severed Foot
entries.text: Wounds: 5. Lose the foot, Amputation (Hard -2 SL); gain 3 Bleeding, 2 Stunned and Prone.

entries.name: Cut Tendon
entries.text: Wounds: 5. Gain 2 Bleeding, 2 Stunned and Prone; leg permanently unusable, Amputation (Very Hard -3 SL).

entries.name: Shattered Pelvis
entries.text: Wounds: Death. Instant death from traumatic shock after pelvic destruction and loss of a leg.

entries.name: Animalistic Legs
entries.text: +1 Movement

entries.name: Corpulent
entries.text: +5 Strength, +5 Toughness, -1 Movement

entries.name: Distended Digits
entries.text: +10 Dexterity

rows.name: Cool
textFields: Stay composed under pressure, resist Fear, maintain resolve and oppose Charm, Intimidate or other Psychology effects (p. 183).

rows.name: Dodge
textFields: Evade hazards or attacks by moving out of their path; commonly used to oppose attacks and avoid combat Damage.

rows.name: Drive
textFields: Control road vehicles, including carts, coaches and unusual engineered vehicles.

rows.name: Endurance
textFields: Withstand deprivation, prolonged effort and hostile environments. Also resists/removes Conditions (p. 184) and assists Wound recovery (p. 170).

rows.name: Navigation
textFields: Find routes across wilderness or sea using landmarks, stars, maps or charts.

rows.name: Outdoor Survival
textFields: Live off the land: hunt, fish, forage, build shelter/fire, read approaching weather and recognise animal traces, including with few tools.

rows.name: Gamble
textFields: Assess wagers and play games of chance. Cheating uses the separate procedure on p. 135.

rows.name: Gossip
textFields: Gather useful news or circulate rumours, typically where people gather.

rows.name: Haggle
textFields: Negotiate a better bargain, usually through Opposed Haggle (p. 131).

rows.name: Heal
textFields: A successful Test can identify illness, treat disease, restore Wounds or stop Bleeding. Illness, injury and treatment procedures appear on p. 172.

rows.name: Intimidate
textFields: Pressure or frighten thinking creatures through explicit or implied threats.

rows.name: Pray
textFields: Communicate with or petition a deity; divine-intervention procedures use Chapter 7.

rows.name: Sail

rows.name: Perception

rows.name: Accurate Shot
textFields: Successful Ranged Attacks deal +1 Damage, or +2 if you aimed (p. 167).

rows.name: Acute Sense (Sense)
textFields: Choose one of the five senses. The GM may allow Perception Tests using it to notice details normally beyond perception. Each further purchase selects a different sense.

rows.name: Aethyric Attunement
textFields: On a Minor Miscast, roll twice and choose either result. A second purchase grants the same choice on Major Miscasts.

rows.name: Alley Cat
textFields: Gain Advantage on Stealth (Urban) Tests. In a familiar settlement, identify its fastest or least conspicuous routes without a Test.

rows.name: Ambidextrous
textFields: Ignore the −2 SL penalty for Tests relying only on your secondary hand, including attacks with a weapon held there.

rows.name: Animal Affinity
textFields: Wild animals normally leave you alone while you show no aggression towards them.

rows.name: Arcane Magic (Lore)
textFields:
Choose a Colour Lore (Beasts, Death, Fire, Heavens, Life, Light, Metal or Shadows), Witch Lore such as Hedgecraft or Witchcraft, or Dark Lore such as Daemonology or Necromancy. Gain one chosen spell in that Lore and access to memorise more. Normally only one Arcane Lore is allowed; with GM permission and suitable study, one Dark Lore may be added to another Arcane Lore. Pay 100 XP to unlearn the Talent, immediately losing its spells.

| Spells already known | XP for next spell |
| --- | --- |
| Up to 5 | 100 |
| 6–10 | 200 |
| 11–15 | 300 |
| 16–20 | 400 |
| 21+ | 500 |

rows.name: Argumentative
textFields: To leave a pointless argument with you, the other person must win Cool Opposed by your Charm. While arguing, they suffer −3 SL to most Tests unrelated to you until attacked or alerted to something more important.

rows.name: Artistic (Art)
textFields: Choose an art form, such as painting or poetry. Gain Advantage on Art Tests in that medium and may always Advance Art regardless of Career. Each further purchase chooses a different form.

rows.name: Attractive
textFields: After a successful Charm Test on someone attracted to you, choose either the rolled SL or your units-die result as SL.

rows.name: Battle Rage
textFields: When another ability permits Frenzy (p. 184), enter it without a Test. Ending Frenzy causes no Fatigued Condition.

rows.name: Beat Blade
textFields: After a successful Melee Attack, you may forgo Damage. Until the opponent’s next Turn ends, they cannot Oppose Melee Tests with a Melee Skill, and Melee Attacks against them gain Advantage. Dodge remains available. Does not work against a larger opponent (p. 360).

rows.name: Beneath Notice
textFields: With suitable clothing and behaviour, people generally assume you belong, including in the presence of social superiors. A plausible explanation satisfies gate guards or similar questions. Drawing attention through a blunder, weapon or other conspicuous action ends this protection.

rows.name: Blather
textFields: When caught where you should not be or doing something improper, make Charm Opposed by Cool. Success makes the target accept your explanation for one Turn or minute per SL, as appropriate. If SL exceed their Willpower Bonus, belief lasts until someone points out its inconsistency.

rows.name: Bless (Deity)
textFields: Gain all Blessings of your deity. Normally only one Bless (Deity) Talent is allowed. Bless is incompatible, in either direction, with Channelling, Arcane Magic, Chaos Magic, Magic Resistance, Petty Magic and Witch! Unlearning costs 100 XP, removes all its Blessings and may incur divine displeasure determined by the GM.

rows.name: Break and Enter
textFields: By observing a building, locked room or vault, identify its apparently quickest and quietest entry. Gain Advantage on Pick Lock and Strength Tests to force doors or windows.

rows.name: Briber
textFields: A brief conversation reveals whether someone accepts bribes and the amount needed for cooperation or silence. Gain Advantage on Bribery Tests.

rows.name: Cardsharp
textFields: On a double in an Opposed Gamble Test, you may reroll the opponent’s Test and cancel any advantage they gained through Sleight of Hand.

rows.name: Careful Strike
textFields: Melee Called Shots suffer only −1 SL, or no penalty when attacking with Advantage.

rows.name: Carouser
textFields: Modest drinking causes no ill effects or Consume Alcohol Tests; test only when drinking excessively. Gain Advantage on Consume Alcohol Tests and Endurance Tests against poison.

rows.name: Catfall
textFields: Treat every fall as deliberate, allowing an Athletics Test to reduce Damage. Athletics Tests made while falling gain Advantage.

rows.name: Cat-tongued
textFields: Gain Advantage on Charm Tests to lie convincingly.

rows.name: Chaos Magic (Lore)
textFields:
Gain one chosen spell from your selected Chaos Lore and access to memorise more. Each spell gained from it causes one Corruption Point. Normally only one Chaos Lore is allowed. This Talent cannot be unlearned.

| Spells already known | XP for next spell |
| --- | --- |
| Up to 5 | 100 |
| 6–10 | 200 |
| 11–15 | 300 |
| 16–20 | 400 |
| 21+ | 500 |

rows.name: Combat Aware
textFields: Pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Perception Test to avoid Surprised. If the GM would already allow a Test to avoid Surprise, succeed automatically.

rows.name: Combat Master
textFields: Count as two people when outnumbering an enemy or determining whether your side is outnumbered (p. 167).

rows.name: Combat Reflexes
textFields: Roll Combat Initiative twice and choose either result.

rows.name: Commanding Presence
textFields: Without an established authority in a crisis, people usually look to you and obey reasonable orders. Gain Advantage on Leadership Tests.

rows.name: Concoct
textFields: Once per session, take a free Crafting Endeavour with Trade (Apothecary, Herbalist or Poisoner) without a Workshop; Trade Tools and materials remain required. The creation expires at the next Downtime’s start, complete or otherwise.

rows.name: Contortionist
textFields: At the GM’s discretion, squeeze through gaps normally difficult or impossible. Gain Advantage on Athletics Tests to escape restraints.

rows.name: Coolheaded
textFields: Gain +5 Willpower. This does not count toward Advances.

rows.name: Crack the Whip
textFields: With Drive, direct your vehicle’s animals to take an Action as well as a Move without a Test. Required Drive Tests gain Advantage. In a vehicle Pursuit, add +1 to the animals’ Movement.

rows.name: Craftsman (Trade)
textFields: Choose a Trade specialisation. Gain Advantage on its Tests and may Advance it regardless of Career. Each further purchase selects a different Trade.

rows.name: Criminal
textFields: Double coin from successful criminal Income Endeavours. Law enforcers regard you suspiciously and criminals recognise you as one of them. You cannot enter a Career whose path lacks Criminal. With GM approval, pay 100 XP to remove this Talent.

rows.name: Deadeye Shot
textFields: Ranged Called Shots suffer only −1 SL, or no penalty if aimed (p. 167).

rows.name: Dealmaker
textFields: Gain Advantage on Haggle Tests and usually recognise when an offer cannot improve.

rows.name: Detect Artefact
textFields: Touch identifies whether an item contains magic. With Second Sight, an Intuition Test can reveal its exact powers, activation and remaining charges.

rows.name: Dirty Fighting
textFields: If an unarmed Called Shot to the body causes any Wounds, you may replace normal Damage with the Low Blow! Critical Wound (p. 175).

rows.name: Disarm
textFields: After a successful attacking melee strike, forgo Damage to knock a held weapon 1d10 feet in a random direction. You may lose Momentum to catch it. Does not affect unarmed opponents, securely attached weapons or larger opponents (p. 360).

rows.name: Distract
textFields: After a successful Melee Attack, forgo Damage to remove the target’s Momentum. Until your next Turn ends, it cannot regain Momentum or gain Advantage on a Test from any other cause.

rows.name: Doomed
textFields: At age 10, a doomsayer of Morr foretold your death during the Dooming. Agree a Doom with the GM. Dying as foretold immediately refreshes every ally’s Fortune and gives your next character one additional starting Fate.

rows.name: Drilled
textFields: Allies may freely Disengage from opponents you are also Engaged with. On your Turn, lose Momentum to give Momentum to shoulder-to-shoulder allies who also have Drilled.

rows.name: Dual Wielder
textFields: When fighting with two weapons (p. 167), the second weapon’s free attack costs no Momentum. Daggers, Knives and similar weapons you wield also gain Parry in this situation.

rows.name: Embezzle
textFields: When Earning in play or through Income, substitute Bribery or Evaluate for the normal Earning Skill to embezzle. Success doubles earnings; failure exposes irregularities and leaves you earning nothing while concealing them.

rows.name: Enclosed Fighter
textFields: Ignore Melee penalties from confined spaces. You may Dodge even where space would normally prevent it.

rows.name: Etiquette (Social Group)
textFields: Choose a social group, such as Criminals, Cultists, Guilders, Nobles or Soldiers. Appropriate dress and behaviour let you blend in; the GM may warn you when your behaviour would breach that group’s customs.

rows.name: Fast Hands
textFields: Use Sleight of Hand to entertain with appearing or vanishing small objects. Gain Advantage on Sleight of Hand and on Melee (Brawling) Tests to touch an opponent, including for spells.

rows.name: Fast Shot
textFields: While not Engaged, make one attack with a loaded Pistol-Trait weapon before the Round’s first turn. It consumes your Action for that Round. Resolve multiple Fast Shots in Combat Initiative order. On your turn, act normally but make no further attack.

rows.name: Fearless (Enemy)
textFields: Choose an enemy group, such as Giants, Skeletons or Trolls, and become immune to fear it causes. Each further purchase chooses another group.

rows.name: Feint
textFields: When attacking in melee with Advantage against an opponent without it, you may force them to defend using Intuition instead of another Skill or Characteristic.

rows.name: Field Dressing
textFields: Gain Advantage on Heal Tests and easily make basic bandages or splints from ordinary materials.

rows.name: Fisherman
textFields: With suitable fishing equipment and sufficient water, catch enough food for yourself plus Initiative Bonus other people. Normal foraging can secure additional fish (p. 152).

rows.name: Flagellant
textFields: Feel no pain and ignore Critical Wound penalties except amputations. If another effect permits Frenzy, suffering a Wound lets you enter it immediately without a Test (p. 184).

rows.name: Flee!
textFields: After Disengaging, immediately make an extra Move away. Choosing to Flee in combat causes no Broken Conditions (p. 163). Gain +1 SL on pursuit Tests as Quarry.

rows.name: Frenzy
textFields: Pass a Willpower Test to enter Frenzy, gaining extra attacks, additional melee Damage and immunity to most psychological effects. See p. 184 for the full Frenzy rules.

rows.name: Frightening
textFields: Gain Fear 1, or Fear 2 if Large (p. 360). Enemies need an Extended Psychology Test with successes equal to Fear Rating, testing once each turn. Until successful, they cannot gain Momentum and your Melee Attacks against them gain Advantage.

rows.name: Furious Assault
textFields: Once per Round after hitting in melee, lose Momentum to make an immediate extra attack.

rows.name: Gregarious
textFields: Gain Advantage on Gossip Tests and usually recognise a settlement’s likely places for gossip.

rows.name: Gunner
textFields: Ignore Dangerous on Blackpowder, Engineering and Explosive weapons you use.

rows.name: Hardy
textFields: Add Toughness Bonus once more when calculating Wounds.

rows.name: Hatred (Group)
textFields: Choose a group to Hate, such as beastmen, goblins, orcs, monsters, outlaws, Sigmarites, undead or witches. On encountering it, pass a Psychology Test or immediately seek its destruction by the fastest, deadliest means. Against it, gain +1 SL on Melee and Ranged Tests and immunity to its Intimidate and Fear, but not Terror. Full Hatred rules: p. 184.

rows.name: Holy Hatred
textFields: When a Miracle causes Wounds, you may add +2 Wounds.

rows.name: Holy Visions
textFields: Automatically recognise holy ground on entering it, perceive Blessings, Miracles and Chaos Magic cast in sight, and sense an object’s divine power by touching it.

rows.name: Hunter’s Eye
textFields: With sufficient time, proper equipment and well-stocked hunting land, automatically obtain enough game for yourself and Initiative Bonus others. Normal foraging can provide more (p. 152).

rows.name: Impassioned Zeal (Cause)
textFields: Choose a political, religious or philosophical cause. Charm Tests advocating it gain Advantage; lying about or denouncing it causes Disadvantage.

rows.name: Implacable
textFields: Whenever you would gain Bleeding Conditions, gain one fewer.

rows.name: In-fighter
textFields: As an Action, make an Opposed Melee Test to close inside the enemy’s reach. The winner chooses normal combat or in-fighting. In-fighting makes weapons longer than Short count as Improvised. An opponent can end it at their Turn’s start by losing Momentum.

rows.name: Inspiring
textFields: Gain Advantage on Leadership Tests in combat.

rows.name: Instinctive Diction
textFields: You may subtract 20 from a Minor Miscast table result; below 01, no Miscast occurs. Major Miscasts are unaffected.

rows.name: Invoke (Deity)
textFields: Gain one chosen Miracle of your deity and access to memorise further available Miracles at their listed XP costs. Normally only one Invoke (Deity) is allowed. Invoke is incompatible, in either direction, with Channelling, Arcane Magic, Chaos Magic, Magic Resistance, Petty Magic and Witch! Unlearning costs 100 XP, removes all its Miracles and incurs extreme divine displeasure determined by the GM.

rows.name: Iron Jaw
textFields: The first time each encounter that you would gain Stunned Conditions, gain one fewer.

rows.name: Iron Will
textFields: Gain Advantage on Cool Tests against others’ influence, including Fellowship Tests and magic.

rows.name: Jump Up
textFields: Gain Advantage on Perform (Acrobatics) Tests to entertain or move quickly outside combat. Upon gaining Prone, immediately attempt a Challenging (+0 SL) Athletics or Perform (Acrobatics) Test to stand.

rows.name: Kingpin
textFields: Criminal no longer makes law enforcers suspicious or restricts Career access. Other criminals usually respect you, except prepared rivals seeking your position.

rows.name: Lightning Reflexes
textFields: Gain +5 Agility. This does not count toward Advances.

rows.name: Linguistics
textFields: Gain Advantage on Language Tests. Every Advance in a Language specialisation costs 50 XP regardless of previous Advances. Language (Magick) is excluded: this applies only to languages used for communication.

rows.name: Lip Reading
textFields: With a clear view of a speaker’s mouth, pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Intuition Test to read their words.

rows.name: Luck
textFields: Increase maximum Fortune by 1. May be purchased three times, for a total +3.

rows.name: Magic Resistance
textFields: Reduce the SL of every spell affecting you by 3. This Talent is mutually exclusive with Channelling, Arcane Magic, Bless, Chaos Magic, Invoke, Petty Magic and Witch!

rows.name: Magical Sense
textFields: Automatically notice spellcasting within Perception yards and its rough direction, but not its nature. With Second Sight or another way to perceive the Winds, gain Advantage on Tests to interpret their behaviour or movement.

rows.name: Magnum Opus
textFields: Each purchase lets you create one extraordinary masterwork using an Art or Trade Skill. It grants GM-determined bonuses, usually to Fellowship Tests involving people who have seen it. Selling it yields at least ten times normal value. Further purchases create additional masterworks.

rows.name: Marksman
textFields: Gain +5 Ballistic Skill. This does not count toward Advances.

rows.name: Master of Disguise
textFields: Change posture, facial expression and suitable clothing to disguise your appearance. On successful Entertain (Acting) Tests, choose rolled SL or the units-die result as SL.

rows.name: Master Orator
textFields: Gain Advantage on Lore (Law) Tests to plead before a magistrate and equivalent Lore Tests to argue academic, religious or political matters before an audience.

rows.name: Master Tradesman (Trade)
textFields: Choose a Trade specialisation. On successful Tests with it, use either rolled SL or the units-die result as SL. Further purchases choose different Trades.

rows.name: Menacing
textFields: Gain Advantage on Intimidation Tests. Sensible thieves, bandits and pickpockets usually choose another available target.

rows.name: Mimic
textFields: Gain Advantage on Entertain (Acting, Comedy) and Perform (Clowning). After hearing an accent for a day, reproduce it, with any local benefits set by the GM. Recognise attempts to conceal or imitate familiar accents unless the speaker also has Mimic.

rows.name: Night Vision
textFields: With even faint light, see clearly for 20 yards and extend light sources’ effective illumination by 20 yards.

rows.name: Nimble-fingered
textFields: Gain +5 Dexterity. This does not count toward Advances.

rows.name: Noble Blood
textFields: When appropriately dressed, count as at least one Status Tier above anyone without Noble Blood. Against others with it, compare Status normally. Enter Noble as though it shared your current Class.

rows.name: Nose for Trouble
textFields: Gain Advantage on Intuition Tests and usually locate opportunities for gambling, fighting or heavy drinking in a settlement.

rows.name: Numismatics
textFields: Gain Advantage on Lore (Heraldry) Tests identifying the origin of coins, medals and flags. After a successful Evaluate Test to value an item, choose rolled SL or the units-die result as SL.

rows.name: Old Salt
textFields: On successful ocean Row or Sail Tests, choose rolled SL or the units-die result as SL. Count as two boatmen towards an ocean-going vessel’s minimum crew.

rows.name: Orientation
textFields: Gain Advantage on Navigation Tests. A glimpse of familiar signs, such as stars or trees, automatically reveals north.

rows.name: Panhandle
textFields: Gain Advantage on begging Charm Tests, including Income Endeavours. Usually find safe but uncomfortable urban sleeping places, such as beneath bridges or near middens.

rows.name: Perfect Pitch
textFields: Learn music after hearing it once. Gain Advantage on Entertain (Singing) and Play (Any) Tests.

rows.name: Petty Magic
textFields:
Gain Willpower Bonus Petty spells on learning this Talent. Additional spells use the prices below; see Chapter 8: Magic. Unlearning costs 100 XP and immediately removes every spell linked to it.

| Spells already known | XP for next spell |
| --- | --- |
| Up to 5 | 50 |
| 6–10 | 100 |
| 11–15 | 150 |
| 16–20 | 200 |
| 21+ | 250 |

rows.name: Pharmacist
textFields: Creating an alchemical remedy produces one additional dose (p. 154).

rows.name: Pilot
textFields: Gain Advantage on Row and Sail Tests.

rows.name: Public Speaker
textFields: Easily gather a crowd and usually judge its mood and motivations. Gain Advantage on Charm Tests to influence groups. Once Charmed, the group can be influenced through Leadership, including urging action or removing Broken (p. 169).

rows.name: Pure Soul
textFields: Double the normal Corruption Point threshold before testing against mutation (p. 188).

rows.name: Rapid Reload
textFields: Reduce your weapon’s Reload Rating by 1.

rows.name: Reaction Strike
textFields: When Charged, pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Initiative Test to make one immediate free attack against the charger, outside turn order, using your primary-hand weapon. Limit: once per round.

rows.name: Read/Write
textFields: Read and write every language you speak.

rows.name: Relentless
textFields: After an opponent Disengages, test Challenging (+0 SL) Athletics, Drive or Ride at their Turn’s end. Success gives an extra Move to follow and free Disengagement from other opponents. As Pursuer in a Pursuit, gain +1 SL on chase Tests.

rows.name: Resistant (Threat)
textFields: Choose a Threat, such as Disease, Magic, Corruption or Poison. Once per session, before rolling against that Threat, choose automatic success; further Tests against it gain Advantage. Further purchases select different Threats.

rows.name: Resolute
textFields: When gaining a Condition, pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Cool Test to keep Momentum.

rows.name: Reversal
textFields: In an Opposed Melee Test, retain Momentum if struck despite your own Test succeeding.

rows.name: Riposte
textFields: Winning an Opposed Test while defending in melee lets you deal Damage as the attacker.

rows.name: River Guide
textFields: Navigate dangerous river water without a Test unless Difficulty is Difficult (−1 SL) or harder. With the matching Lore (Local), no navigation Test is required: you know a safe route.

rows.name: Robust
textFields: When testing to heal Wounds, you may recover 2 extra Wounds.

rows.name: Roughrider
textFields: With Ride, direct your mount to take an Action as well as a Move without a Ride Test. Required Ride Tests gain Advantage. Mounted Pursuits add +1 to the animal’s Movement.

rows.name: Rover
textFields: Gain Advantage on Stealth (Rural). Usually identify easy routes through wilderness and sources of game, water and shelter.

rows.name: Savant (Lore Specialisation)
textFields: Choose a Lore specialisation you possess and gain Advantage on its Tests. Each further purchase selects a different Lore.

rows.name: Savvy
textFields: Gain +5 Intelligence. This does not count toward Advances.

rows.name: Scale Sheer Surface
textFields: Gain Advantage on Climb Tests. You may attempt apparently impossible surfaces, including sheer walls, ice and greased poles, with no imposed Difficulty harder than Very Hard (−3 SL).

rows.name: Schemer
textFields: After successful Gossip or Lore (Politics) Tests, choose rolled SL or the units-die result as SL.

rows.name: Sea Legs
textFields: Normal sea conditions require no seasickness Test. When the GM does require one, gain Advantage.

rows.name: Seasoned Traveller
textFields: While in a region, you may always Advance its Lore (Local), regardless of Career.

rows.name: Secret Identity
textFields: Adopt a persona with a chosen Career for an encounter, day, adventure or other set period without testing to maintain it. Use that Career’s Class and Status, including for Banking or Income Endeavours. Income requires a Challenging (+0 SL) Earning Test with Entertain (Acting) or the assumed Career’s Earning Skill, rather than your real Career’s. With Embezzle, Bribery or Evaluate may replace it when embezzling. Failure exposes the deception, with GM-determined consequences.

rows.name: Shadow
textFields: If someone you follow passes a Perception Test to detect you, choose to remain unseen and lose them, or keep following and be spotted.

rows.name: Sharp
textFields: Gain +5 Initiative. This does not count toward Advances.

rows.name: Sharpshooter
textFields: Ignore Ranged penalties from Prone targets and cover. Extraordinary accuracy feats remain possible with a successful Ranged Test at GM-set Difficulty.

rows.name: Shieldsman
textFields: Once per Round while carrying a shield, lose Momentum either to grant its AP bonus to an adjacent ally without a shield or, after winning an attacking or defending Opposed Melee Test, to push the opponent up to 2 yards directly away and end engagement.

rows.name: Sixth Sense
textFields: Just before triggering a trap or suffering hidden danger, pass a Challenging (+0 SL) Intuition Test to notice it at the final moment.

rows.name: Slayer
textFields: Charging a creature larger than you automatically grants Momentum.

rows.name: Small
textFields: Gain Size (Small); full Size rules are on p. 360 in Chapter 12: Bestiary.

rows.name: Sniper
textFields: Ignore Long Range shooting penalties. Extreme Range shots suffer only −1 SL.

rows.name: Speedreader
textFields: Read a full page at a glance and even a long book in a day. Double SL from successful Tests in an Extended Research Test.

rows.name: Sprinter
textFields: Gain Advantage on Athletics Tests to run or jump.

rows.name: Step Aside
textFields: After successfully Dodging an attack, move up to 2 yards and end engagement without granting opponents free attacks.

rows.name: Stone Soup
textFields: A party member’s Foraging Test automatically finds enough extra food for you, even on failure, beyond whoever the result normally feeds (p. 152).

rows.name: Stout-hearted
textFields: The first time each encounter you gain Broken Conditions, gain one fewer.

rows.name: Striding Gait (Terrain)
textFields: Choose terrain, such as Coastal, Desert, Rocky, Tundra, Wetland or Woodland. Ignore its movement penalties and gain +2 SL to all Pursuit-related Tests there. Further purchases select different terrain.

rows.name: Strike Mighty Blow
textFields: Melee weapons deal +1 Damage, or +2 when the attack has Advantage.

rows.name: Strike to Injure
textFields: Roll twice on Critical Wound tables and choose either result. Silent Takedowns also ignore the Called Shot penalty (p. 135).

rows.name: Strike to Stun
textFields: Improvised Weapons gain Pummel. With a Pummel weapon, ignore the Silent Takedown Called Shot penalty (p. 135).

rows.name: Strong Back
textFields: Gain +1 SL on Opposed Strength Tests and carry +1 Encumbrance. A second purchase raises both totals to +3.

rows.name: Strong Legs
textFields: On successful Athletics Tests to sprint or leap, choose rolled SL or the units-die result as SL.

rows.name: Strong-minded
textFields: Once per session, before a Test, choose to ignore all its negative modifiers.

rows.name: Strong Swimmer
textFields: Gain Advantage on Swim Tests and +2 SL in swimming Pursuits.

rows.name: Sturdy
textFields: Count Strength Bonus twice when calculating carrying capacity in Encumbrance Points.

rows.name: Suave
textFields: Gain +5 Fellowship. This does not count toward Advances.

rows.name: Super Numerate
textFields: Calculate most mathematical problems without tools. Gain Advantage on Evaluate Tests and accurately track elapsed time while conscious.

rows.name: Supportive
textFields: Ignore penalties for Charming higher Status Tiers, and gain Advantage on Charm Tests to ingratiate yourself with higher-Status people.

rows.name: Sure Shot
textFields: Ranged Attacks deal +1 Damage and may ignore Partial armour. Impale weapons may also ignore Weakpoints armour.

rows.name: Surgery
textFields: On successful Heal Tests outside combat, choose rolled SL or the units-die result as SL. Treat Critical Wounds requiring Surgery; see pp. 172–179 for effects.

rows.name: Tenacious
textFields: The first time each encounter you would gain Fatigued Conditions, gain one fewer.

rows.name: Tinker
textFields: For repairs, treat every Trade as Basic. With at least one Advance in the relevant Trade, repair Tests gain Advantage and take half normal time.

rows.name: Tower of Memories
textFields: Store facts in an imagined tower to recall them precisely. On successful Lore Tests, choose rolled SL or the units-die result as SL.

rows.name: Trapper
textFields: Gain Advantage on Set Trap Tests. With one hour of preparation, build a small animal trap or covered pit from available materials (p. 136).

rows.name: Trick Rider
textFields: While mounted, use any Perform Skill and Dodge without modification.

rows.name: Tunnel Fighter
textFields: Gain Advantage on Stealth (Underground). Easily estimate distance travelled underground and depth below ground.

rows.name: Unshakeable
textFields: Being shot at with a Blackpowder weapon requires no Test to resist Broken.

rows.name: Very Resilient
textFields: Gain +5 Toughness. This does not count toward Advances.

rows.name: Very Strong
textFields: Gain +5 Strength. This does not count toward Advances.

rows.name: War Leader
textFields: Allies affected by your battlefield Leadership may use it instead of Cool against Fear until the battle ends (p. 169). This ends if you die and is suspended while you have Broken, Unconscious or Fear Conditions.

rows.name: Warrior Born
textFields: Gain +5 Weapon Skill. This does not count toward Advances.

rows.name: War Wizard
textFields: On your Turn, cast one spell of CN 5 or less without using your Action. You cannot cast another spell that Turn.

rows.name: Waterman
textFields: On successful Row or Sail Tests on rivers or lakes, choose rolled SL or the units-die result as SL. Count as two crew towards a river vessel’s minimum crew.

rows.name: Wealthy
textFields: Earning through your Career in play or through Income provides +1 gold crown. A second purchase increases the total bonus to +3 gold crowns.

rows.name: Well-prepared
textFields: Once per session, produce a needed Encumbrance 0 Trapping that you could plausibly have bought recently. Deduct its price as an earlier purchase; without money, you cannot use this Talent. Further uses that session cost Fortune.

rows.name: Witch!
textFields: Gain one chosen Colour Lore or Witchcraft spell without needing the matching Arcane Magic, and treat its Channelling Skill as Basic. Another spell with the same benefits costs 150 XP, with each later spell costing 50 XP more. Witch hunters may take interest and established magical orders may present difficulties. Pay 100 XP to remove this Talent and every linked spell.

Gain one chosen spell in that Lore and access to memorise more. Normally only one Arcane Lore is allowed; with GM permission and suitable study, one Dark Lore may be added to another Arcane Lore. rows.name: Arcane Magic (Heavens)
textFields:
Choose a Colour Lore (Beasts, Death, Fire, Heavens, Life, Light, Metal or Shadows), Witch Lore such as Hedgecraft or Witchcraft, or Dark Lore such as Daemonology or Necromancy. Gain one chosen spell in that Lore and access to memorise more. Normally only one Arcane Lore is allowed; with GM permission and suitable study, one Dark Lore may be added to another Arcane Lore. Pay 100 XP to unlearn the Talent, immediately losing its spells.

| Spells already known | XP for next spell |
| --- | --- |
| Up to 5 | 100 |
| 6–10 | 200 |
| 11–15 | 300 |
| 16–20 | 400 |
| 21+ | 500 |

rows.name: Bless (Manann)
textFields: Gain all Blessings of your deity. Normally only one Bless (Deity) Talent is allowed. Bless is incompatible, in either direction, with Channelling, Arcane Magic, Chaos Magic, Magic Resistance, Petty Magic and Witch! Unlearning costs 100 XP, removes all its Blessings and may incur divine displeasure determined by the GM.
